title: Noticing the Present
description: Develop the capacity to notice what is already here, without adding commentary.
short_description: Develop the capacity to notice what is already here, without

content.objective: Develop the capacity to notice what is already here, without adding commentary.
instructions: Sit comfortably and let your eyes close or soften.
Ask: what is present in my awareness right now?
Notice sounds, sensations, the breath — whatever is already here.
When a label or story appears, note 'commentary' and return to raw noticing.
Rest in the bare perception of what is.

session_steps.title: Arrive
session_steps.content: Settle into your seat. Feel the contact points with the chair or floor.

session_steps.title: Notice
session_steps.content: Let awareness rest on whatever is already present — no choosing, no rejecting.

session_steps.title: Note
session_steps.content: When commentary arises, silently note 'commentary' and return to bare perception.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest as the one who notices.

content.expected_experience: The present moment reveals itself as already complete — busy, quiet, or chaotic, but always here to be noticed.
content.safety_notes: Safe for everyone. If noticing becomes overwhelming, open your eyes and name three objects in the room.

title: The Observer's Seat
description: Establish the felt shift from being experience to witnessing it.
short_description: Establish the felt shift from being experience to witnessing

content.objective: Establish the felt shift from being experience to witnessing it.
instructions: Sit with spine erect but not rigid.
Close your eyes and take three settling breaths.
Notice that sounds are heard, thoughts are seen, sensations are felt.
Ask: who is hearing, seeing, feeling?
Do not answer in words. Rest in the knowing itself.
When you forget, the next noticing is the practice.

session_steps.title: Settle
session_steps.content: Three slow breaths. Let the seat hold you.

session_steps.title: Hear
session_steps.content: Listen to the sound field without following any one sound.

session_steps.title: Ask
session_steps.content: Silently ask: who is aware of this?

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest in the not-knowing. The question does its work without an answer.

content.expected_experience: A subtle relocation of identity — from the content of experience to the space in which it appears.
content.safety_notes: If the question creates agitation, return to breath awareness. The question is an invitation, not a demand.

title: Thought Watching
description: Watch thoughts arise and pass like weather, without boarding any of them.
short_description: Watch thoughts arise and pass like weather, without boarding

content.objective: Watch thoughts arise and pass like weather, without boarding any of them.
instructions: Sit quietly and close your eyes.
Let thoughts come and go without following them.
When you notice you have been carried away, note 'thinking' and return.
Watch the gap between one thought and the next.
Notice that you were always the watcher, never the thought.

session_steps.title: Settle
session_steps.content: Two minutes of breath settling.

session_steps.title: Watch
session_steps.content: Observe thoughts like clouds crossing an open sky.

session_steps.title: Gap
session_steps.content: Look for the pause between thoughts. Even a fraction of a second counts.

session_steps.title: Note
session_steps.content: What did you notice about the mind's habits?

content.expected_experience: Thoughts lose their authority when watched. Many report a growing gap between impulse and identification.
contraindications: acute psychosis — practice with a professional
content.safety_notes: If watching thoughts increases distress, shift to body awareness or open eyes. Do not suppress thoughts; watch them.

title: Emotion Observation
description: Observe emotion as a moving pattern in the body, separate from its story.
short_description: Observe emotion as a moving pattern in the body, separate fr

content.objective: Observe emotion as a moving pattern in the body, separate from its story.
instructions: Bring to mind a mildly charged situation, or wait for whatever emotion is present.
Locate the emotion in the body — chest, throat, belly, shoulders.
Describe the sensation neutrally: tight, warm, heavy, buzzing.
Watch the emotion's intensity change on its own.
Notice: the emotion is not you; it is something you are aware of.

session_steps.title: Arrive
session_steps.content: Settle. Scan the body for any emotional signature.

session_steps.title: Locate
session_steps.content: Find where the emotion lives in the body. Rest attention there.

session_steps.title: Describe
session_steps.content: Silently describe sensation qualities without interpretation.

session_steps.title: Watch Change
session_steps.content: Observe intensity rise, fall, or shift. Do nothing about it.

session_steps.title: Note
session_steps.content: What changed when you observed rather than reacted?

content.expected_experience: Emotions become workable objects of awareness rather than commands. Most people feel a new spaciousness around feeling.
contraindications: recent trauma — use titration: 2-3 minutes only, with grounding after
content.safety_notes: Choose mild charge. If overwhelm rises, return to the feet and the room. This is observation, not excavation.

title: Sensory Observation
description: Open all five senses to the present moment without preference.
short_description: Open all five senses to the present moment without preferenc

content.objective: Open all five senses to the present moment without preference.
instructions: Sit or stand wherever you are. Let your eyes open softly.
Notice five things you can see, without evaluating them.
Notice four things you can hear.
Notice three things you can touch.
Notice two things you can smell, and one you can taste.
Let all five senses rest together in one field of awareness.

session_steps.title: See
session_steps.content: Five visual observations, no opinions attached.

session_steps.title: Hear
session_steps.content: Four sounds, near and far.

session_steps.title: Feel
session_steps.content: Three tactile sensations.

session_steps.title: Smell & Taste
session_steps.content: Two scents, one taste (even if just the mouth's own taste).

session_steps.title: Unify
session_steps.content: Hold all senses in one open awareness.

content.expected_experience: The world becomes vivid and immediate. The mind's commentary quiets when the senses are fully employed.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. A powerful grounding tool during anxiety.

title: Sound Field Listening
description: Hear the entire sound field as one texture, without chasing individual sounds.
short_description: Hear the entire sound field as one texture, without chasing

content.objective: Hear the entire sound field as one texture, without chasing individual sounds.
instructions: Close your eyes and let hearing open.
Notice the nearest sound, then the farthest.
Notice silence between sounds.
Let all sounds arrive as one field — no foreground, no background.
When a sound triggers a story, return to pure hearing.

session_steps.title: Open Hearing
session_steps.content: Let sounds come to you. Do not look for them.

session_steps.title: Near and Far
session_steps.content: Map the sound field from nearest to farthest.

session_steps.title: Silence
session_steps.content: Notice the silence that allows sound to be heard.

session_steps.title: Field
session_steps.content: Rest as the space in which all sounds appear.

content.expected_experience: Sound stops being noise and becomes texture. Many notice the silence 'between' sounds for the first time.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. In loud environments, keep volume comfortable — this is about attention, not endurance.

title: Body Sensation Watching
description: Observe bodily sensations with the neutrality of a scientist.
short_description: Observe bodily sensations with the neutrality of a scientist

content.objective: Observe bodily sensations with the neutrality of a scientist.
instructions: Sit still and close your eyes.
Scan the body from feet to head, noting sensation in each region.
Classify nothing as good or bad — only intensity, location, quality.
Watch sensations that were below the threshold of attention all day.
Notice how sensations change when watched.

session_steps.title: Scan
session_steps.content: Slow sweep from feet to crown, one region at a time.

session_steps.title: Neutral Note
session_steps.content: Describe each sensation with neutral words: pulsing, warm, numb, vibrating.

session_steps.title: Threshold
session_steps.content: Find one sensation you had not noticed before today.

session_steps.title: Observe Change
session_steps.content: Watch how attention itself alters sensation.

content.expected_experience: The body reveals itself as a living field of sensation. Chronic tensions often become visible for the first time.
contraindications: acute pain conditions — skip painful regions
content.safety_notes: Do not try to change anything. Observation only. Pain is information, not a project to fix.

title: Impulse Watching
description: Notice impulses (to move, check, speak, eat) without obeying or suppressing them.
short_description: Notice impulses (to move, check, speak, eat) without obeying

content.objective: Notice impulses (to move, check, speak, eat) without obeying or suppressing them.
instructions: Sit still with eyes closed or softly open.
Wait for the next impulse — to shift, scratch, check a phone, speak.
Notice the impulse as a sensation before it becomes action.

title: Judgment Watching
description: Observe the judging mind at work, without becoming the judge of your judging.
short_description: Observe the judging mind at work, without becoming the judge

content.objective: Observe the judging mind at work, without becoming the judge of your judging.
instructions: Sit quietly and let the mind do what it does.
Notice evaluations: good, bad, better, worse, should, shouldn't.
Label each one silently: 'judging'.
Watch the judge itself — who is judging the judge?
Let judgments pass like traffic. You are the road, not the cars.

session_steps.title: Listen
session_steps.content: Listen to the mind's evaluative commentary.

session_steps.title: Label
session_steps.content: Silently mark each judgment: 'judging'.

session_steps.title: Watch the Judge
session_steps.content: Turn attention toward the one who judges.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest as the space that holds all judgment without being it.

content.expected_experience: Judgment loses its sting when seen as a mechanical habit. Self-acceptance often arrives on its own.
content.safety_notes: If self-judgment becomes harsh, switch to compassion practice. Observation is not self-criticism.

title: Beginner's Eyes
description: See the familiar environment as if for the first time.
short_description: See the familiar environment as if for the first time.

content.objective: See the familiar environment as if for the first time.
instructions: Choose one ordinary object in the room — a cup, a door, a plant.
Look at it as if you have never seen it before.
Notice its color gradients, edges, weight, texture.
Ask: what have I never noticed about this object?
Extend the same fresh looking to the whole room.

session_steps.title: Choose
session_steps.content: Pick one ordinary object.

session_steps.title: First Look
session_steps.content: Look with total freshness — no name, no use, just form.

session_steps.title: Detail
session_steps.content: Find three details you have never noticed.

session_steps.title: Expand
session_steps.content: Extend beginner's eyes to the entire room.

content.expected_experience: The ordinary world becomes strange and rich again. Attention itself feels refreshed.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Who Is Thinking?
description: Turn attention back to the source of thoughts using Ramana Maharshi's direct inquiry.
short_description: Turn attention back to the source of thoughts using Ramana M

content.objective: Turn attention back to the source of thoughts using Ramana Maharshi's direct inquiry.
instructions: Sit quietly and let thoughts arise naturally.
The moment you notice a thought, ask: 'Who is thinking this?'
Do not answer with words. Look for the thinker.
If no thinker is found, rest in that not-finding.
Repeat with each new thought. The practice is the looking.

session_steps.title: Settle
session_steps.content: One minute of natural breathing.

session_steps.title: Wait
session_steps.content: Let a thought appear on its own.

session_steps.title: Inquire
session_steps.content: 'Who is thinking this?' — look, don't theorize.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest in the silence after the question.

content.expected_experience: The thinker is rarely found. In the not-finding, identification with thought loosens — sometimes dramatically.
content.safety_notes: If inquiry creates fear or derealization, stop. Return to breath or body awareness. Inquiry is a looking, not a forcing.

content.objective: Turn attention back to the source of thoughts using Ramana Maharshi's direct inquiry. (Gentle variation.)
instructions: Sit quietly and let thoughts arise naturally.
The moment you notice a thought, ask: 'Who is thinking this?'
Do not answer with words. Look for the thinker.
If no thinker is found, rest in that not-finding.
Repeat with each new thought. The practice is the looking.

session_steps.title: Settle
session_steps.content: One minute of natural breathing.

session_steps.title: Wait
session_steps.content: Let a thought appear on its own.

session_steps.title: Inquire
session_steps.content: 'Who is thinking this?' — look, don't theorize.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest in the silence after the question.

content.expected_experience: The thinker is rarely found. In the not-finding, identification with thought loosens — sometimes dramatically.
content.safety_notes: If inquiry creates fear or derealization, stop. Return to breath or body awareness. Inquiry is a looking, not a forcing.

title: The Direct Question
description: Hold 'Who am I?' without seeking a verbal answer.
short_description: Hold 'Who am I?' without seeking a verbal answer.

content.objective: Hold 'Who am I?' without seeking a verbal answer.
instructions: Sit with spine erect, eyes closed.
Ask once, slowly: 'Who am I?'
Reject every ready-made answer — name, role, story.
Let the question deepen into a wordless looking.
Stay with the question as a sensation of openness.

session_steps.title: Ask
session_steps.content: Ask 'Who am I?' with full attention, once.

session_steps.title: Reject
session_steps.content: Let each answer arise and fall away — not this, not this.

session_steps.title: Deepen
session_steps.content: The question becomes a posture of openness.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest in the openness the question creates.

content.expected_experience: Identity stops being a conclusion and becomes an open question — unsettling at first, then deeply freeing.
content.safety_notes: If the question triggers identity panic, ground in the body: feel the feet, name the room. Return when settled.

title: Neti Neti Walkthrough
description: Systematically disidentify from every layer of experience — not this, not this.
short_description: Systematically disidentify from every layer of experience —

content.objective: Systematically disidentify from every layer of experience — not this, not this.
instructions: Begin with the body: 'I am not this body' — notice the body as an object of awareness.
Move to emotions: 'I am not these feelings' — watch them change.
Move to thoughts: 'I am not these thoughts' — watch them come and go.
Move to roles: 'I am not this name, this job, this history.'
What remains when every layer is set aside? Rest there.

session_steps.title: Body
session_steps.content: Disidentify from the body — it is observed, not the observer.

session_steps.title: Emotion
session_steps.content: Disidentify from feeling — it changes; you do not.

session_steps.title: Thought
session_steps.content: Disidentify from thinking — it is seen, it is not the seer.

session_steps.title: Story
session_steps.content: Disidentify from roles, names, memories.

session_steps.title: Remainder
session_steps.content: Rest in what cannot be disidentified.

content.expected_experience: A systematic clearing. What remains is not a new identity but the absence of false ones — often experienced as relief.
content.safety_notes: Neti neti is subtraction, not annihilation. If fear arises, return to the body and the breath. The goal is freedom from misidentification, not blankness.

title: Tracing the I-Thought
description: Follow the sense of 'I' back to its source, as taught in the Yoga Vasistha tradition.
short_description: Follow the sense of 'I' back to its source, as taught in the

content.objective: Follow the sense of 'I' back to its source, as taught in the Yoga Vasistha tradition.
instructions: Notice the subtle sense of 'I am' that accompanies every experience.
Ask: where does this 'I' feel located?
Watch whether the 'I' moves, changes, or stays constant.
Try to find its edges — where does 'I' begin and end?
Rest in the 'I am' before any 'I am this'.

session_steps.title: Locate
session_steps.content: Find the felt sense of 'I' right now.

session_steps.title: Examine
session_steps.content: Is it in the head, chest, whole body, nowhere?

session_steps.title: Watch Change
session_steps.content: Does the 'I' change with mood, posture, thought?

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest as 'I am' without any 'this'.

content.expected_experience: The 'I' is found to be elusive — present but unlocatable. This elusiness itself points to awareness without form.
content.safety_notes: If the search becomes obsessive or frightening, stop and name five things you can see. The 'I' question is a pointer, not a trap.

title: Inquiring into Anger

content.objective: Apply self-inquiry to a charged emotion: who is angry, and of what?

Feel anger in the body first, before any story.
Ask: 'Who is angry?' Look for the angry one.
Ask: 'Is the anger me, or is it something I am aware of?'

session_steps.title: Separate
session_steps.content: Anger is observed; the observer is untouched.

content.safety_notes: Use only mild-to-moderate charge. If anger escalates, stop, ground, and return to a regulation practice.

title: The Believer's Inquiry
description: Examine a believed thought: who believes it, and what happens without it?
short_description: Examine a believed thought: who believes it, and what happen

content.objective: Examine a believed thought: who believes it, and what happens without it?
instructions: Write down one stressful belief you hold about yourself or life.
Read it slowly. Notice the sense of truth it carries.
Ask: 'Who would I be without this thought?'
Ask: 'Is this thought absolutely true, always, without exception?'
Rest in the space where the belief is seen as a thought, not a fact.

session_steps.title: Name
session_steps.content: State the belief plainly, in writing or silently.

session_steps.title: Feel
session_steps.content: Notice the body's response to the belief.

session_steps.title: Question
session_steps.content: 'Who believes this? Who would I be without it?'

session_steps.title: Turn
session_steps.content: Find the opposite and notice what it reveals.

content.expected_experience: Beliefs are seen as lenses, not windows. The same world looks different through a loosened belief.
content.safety_notes: Choose one belief at a time. Deep core beliefs are best worked with support — this practice is for noticing, not forcing revision.

title: The Sleeper's Question
description: Inquire into the continuity of awareness across waking, dreaming, and sleep.
short_description: Inquire into the continuity of awareness across waking, drea

content.objective: Inquire into the continuity of awareness across waking, dreaming, and sleep.
instructions: Recall last night's dream — you were there, experiencing it.
Recall deep sleep: no dream, no world, yet 'I slept well.'
Ask: what was aware of the absence of experience?
Notice: the 'I' that reports having slept was not absent.
Rest in the awareness that persists through all three states.

session_steps.title: Dream
session_steps.content: Recall a dream. You were the one who experienced it.

session_steps.title: Sleep
session_steps.content: Recall deep sleep — experience absent, yet 'I' persisted.

session_steps.title: Inquire
session_steps.content: What remained aware through both?

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest as that which never sleeps.

content.expected_experience: A glimpse of awareness as the constant through changing states — the foundation of the Mandukya Upanishad's teaching.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Best practiced rested; sleep deprivation makes the inquiry muddy.

title: The Desire Inquiry
description: Look directly at desire: what is wanted, by whom, and what happens when it is seen?
short_description: Look directly at desire: what is wanted, by whom, and what h

content.objective: Look directly at desire: what is wanted, by whom, and what happens when it is seen?
instructions: Notice a current desire — small or large.
Feel the wanting in the body before any plan to fulfill it.
Ask: 'If I obtain this, what do I expect to feel?'
Ask: 'Is the feeling I seek available now, in the looking?'
Watch desire as energy, not as lack.

session_steps.title: Notice
session_steps.content: Catch a desire in the act of arising.

session_steps.title: Locate
session_steps.content: Where does wanting live in the body?

session_steps.title: Project
session_steps.content: What future feeling is the desire promising?

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest as the one who wants, prior to the wanting.

content.expected_experience: Desire stops being a compulsion and becomes a visible movement. Its grip loosens without suppression.
content.safety_notes: This is observation of desire, not renunciation. Do not try to destroy wanting — understand it.

title: The Fear Inquiry
description: Turn toward fear with inquiry instead of avoidance.
short_description: Turn toward fear with inquiry instead of avoidance.

content.objective: Turn toward fear with inquiry instead of avoidance.
instructions: Bring to mind a mild fear — not a trauma, a daily unease.
Feel fear in the body: where, what quality?
Ask: 'What exactly am I afraid of?' Follow the chain down.
Ask: 'Who is afraid?' Look for the afraid one.
Watch fear as a visitor with a message, not an owner.

session_steps.title: Approach
session_steps.content: Choose a mild fear. Approach it gently.

session_steps.title: Body
session_steps.content: Locate fear's physical signature.

session_steps.title: Chain
session_steps.content: Ask 'what am I afraid of?' three times, going deeper.

session_steps.title: Witness
session_steps.content: 'Who is afraid?' — look for the one who fears.

content.expected_experience: Fear is found to be layered — and each layer is see-through. The core fear of 'I' dissolving softens when witnessed.
contraindications: trauma history — use only mild fears; pair with a trauma-informed professional
content.safety_notes: Mild fears only. If freeze or panic appears, stop, orient to the room, feel the feet. Inquiry is titrated, never flooded.

title: The Freedom Question
description: Inquire into what is already free, prior to any effort to be free.
short_description: Inquire into what is already free, prior to any effort to be

content.objective: Inquire into what is already free, prior to any effort to be free.
instructions: Sit quietly. Notice the effort to be free, to be better, to arrive.
Ask: 'What is already free, right now, without any doing?'
Notice that awareness itself needs no improvement.
Watch the effortful self as an object in awareness.
Rest as the freedom that precedes the search for it.

session_steps.title: Notice Effort
session_steps.content: Feel the subtle striving to progress, fix, arrive.

session_steps.title: Ask
session_steps.content: 'What is already free, without any doing?'

session_steps.title: See
session_steps.content: Awareness itself — ungraspable, unconfined, already here.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest as the freedom that was never absent.

content.expected_experience: The spiritual search itself is seen as an object. What remains is quiet — not achieved, but recognized.
content.safety_notes: If 'nothing matters' nihilism appears, that is resistance — return to the body and compassion practices. Freedom includes the relative world.

title: Witness the Breath
description: Develop the capacity to observe without interfering — the foundation of all awareness practices.
short_description: Develop the capacity to observe without interfering — the fo

content.objective: Develop the capacity to observe without interfering — the foundation of all awareness practices.
instructions: Sit comfortably with spine erect.
Close your eyes or soften your gaze.
Notice the natural rhythm of your breath.
Do not try to change the breath in any way.
When the mind wanders, gently return attention to the breath.
Continue for the full duration.

session_steps.title: Settle
session_steps.content: Find a comfortable seated position.

session_steps.title: Observe
session_steps.content: Watch the breath as it is.

session_steps.title: Notice
session_steps.content: What did you observe about your breath?

content.expected_experience: A sense of calm observation; noticing that you are not the breath but the one watching it.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If you feel dizzy, return to normal breathing.

title: The Silent Witness
description: Abide as the silent one who watches all experience without participating in it.
short_description: Abide as the silent one who watches all experience without p

content.objective: Abide as the silent one who watches all experience without participating in it.
instructions: Sit still and let experience come: sounds, sensations, thoughts.
Take no side. Prefer nothing. Reject nothing.
Notice the quality of awareness itself — silent, still, unaffected.
When emotion or thought demands involvement, remain the witness.
Rest in the silence that watches the noise.

session_steps.title: Open
session_steps.content: Let the field of experience be exactly as it is.

session_steps.title: No Side
session_steps.content: Watch without preference, without interference.

session_steps.title: Quality
session_steps.content: Notice the silence of the witness itself.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest as silence watching noise.

content.expected_experience: A profound neutrality — experience continues, but its power to disturb depends on your identification with it.
content.safety_notes: Witnessing is not dissociation. If numbness appears, return to the body and feel. The witness is intimately present, not absent.

title: The Silent Witness — Evening
description: Abide as the silent one who watches all experience without participating in it.
short_description: Abide as the silent one who watches all experience without p

content.objective: Abide as the silent one who watches all experience without participating in it. (Evening variation.)
instructions: Sit still and let experience come: sounds, sensations, thoughts.
Take no side. Prefer nothing. Reject nothing.
Notice the quality of awareness itself — silent, still, unaffected.
When emotion or thought demands involvement, remain the witness.
Rest in the silence that watches the noise.

session_steps.title: Open
session_steps.content: Let the field of experience be exactly as it is.

session_steps.title: No Side
session_steps.content: Watch without preference, without interference.

session_steps.title: Quality
session_steps.content: Notice the silence of the witness itself.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest as silence watching noise.

content.expected_experience: A profound neutrality — experience continues, but its power to disturb depends on your identification with it.
content.safety_notes: Witnessing is not dissociation. If numbness appears, return to the body and feel. The witness is intimately present, not absent.

title: Sakshi Abiding
description: Abide as Sakshi — the pure witness of Vedanta — through sustained recognition.
short_description: Abide as Sakshi — the pure witness of Vedanta — through sust

content.objective: Abide as Sakshi — the pure witness of Vedanta — through sustained recognition.
instructions: Close your eyes and settle.
Notice that every experience has two sides: the seen and the seer.
Place attention on the seer — the one aware of this very noticing.
Keep the recognition gentle and continuous: 'I am the witness.'
Let experiences come and go within you, as clouds in an unchanging sky.

session_steps.title: Settle
session_steps.content: Two minutes of natural breath.

session_steps.title: Two Sides
session_steps.content: Notice the seen and the seer in every moment.

session_steps.title: Abide
session_steps.content: Rest as the seer. 'I am the witness.'

session_steps.title: Sky
session_steps.content: Experiences are clouds; you are the sky.

content.expected_experience: A stable, quiet recognition that awareness was never engaged in the drama it observes.
content.safety_notes: If the sense of self becomes unstable or frightening, open your eyes, feel the body, and return to ordinary awareness. Recognition is gentle, never forced.

title: Witness of Emotions
description: Watch emotions arise and dissolve without becoming their author or their victim.
short_description: Watch emotions arise and dissolve without becoming their aut

content.objective: Watch emotions arise and dissolve without becoming their author or their victim.
instructions: Sit quietly and scan for whatever emotion is present — even subtle.
Give it no name at first; just feel its shape.
Then name it precisely: irritation, tenderness, boredom, longing.
Watch its texture change — emotions are processes, not possessions.
Notice the one who watches is untouched by the weather.

session_steps.title: Scan
session_steps.content: Find the emotion present right now, however subtle.

session_steps.title: Shape
session_steps.content: Feel its bodily shape before naming it.

session_steps.title: Name
session_steps.content: Name it precisely — precision itself is liberating.

session_steps.title: Watch Change
session_steps.content: Observe the emotion's natural arc.

content.expected_experience: Emotions are discovered to be temporary visitors with useful messages. The relationship to feeling transforms from ownership to guardianship.
content.safety_notes: For intense or traumatic emotion, keep sessions short and ground afterwards. Witnessing supports regulation; it does not replace therapy.

title: Witness of Pain
description: Observe physical pain as sensation plus resistance, and watch what remains.
short_description: Observe physical pain as sensation plus resistance, and watc

content.objective: Observe physical pain as sensation plus resistance, and watch what remains.
instructions: Sit comfortably. Bring attention to an area of mild discomfort.
Separate the raw sensation from the story about it.
Watch the sensation with curiosity: edges, pulsing, temperature.
Notice the 'I don't want this' — the resistance — as its own sensation.
Watch both, sensation and resistance, as objects in awareness.

session_steps.title: Locate
session_steps.content: Choose an area of mild, stable discomfort.

session_steps.title: Raw Sensation
session_steps.content: Describe the sensation neutrally, without the story.

session_steps.title: Resistance
session_steps.content: Notice the wanting-it-gone as a separate layer.

session_steps.title: Both
session_steps.content: Watch sensation and resistance together.

content.expected_experience: Pain is often found to be sensation plus a second layer of suffering (resistance). Watching both changes the total experience.
contraindications: undiagnosed pain — see a physician first
content.safety_notes: Mild discomfort only. Never practice on acute or severe pain. Stop if pain intensifies. This is a skill for chronic, stable sensation.

Separate the raw sensation from the story about it.
Watch the sensation with curiosity: edges, pulsing, temperature.
Notice the 'I don't want this' — the resistance — as its own sensation.
Watch both, sensation and resistance, as objects in awareness.

session_steps.title: Locate
session_steps.content: Choose an area of mild, stable discomfort.

session_steps.title: Raw Sensation
session_steps.content: Describe the sensation neutrally, without the story.

session_steps.title: Resistance
session_steps.content: Notice the wanting-it-gone as a separate layer.

session_steps.title: Both
session_steps.content: Watch sensation and resistance together.

content.expected_experience: Pain is often found to be sensation plus a second layer of suffering (resistance). Watching both changes the total experience.
contraindications: undiagnosed pain — see a physician first
content.safety_notes: Mild discomfort only. Never practice on acute or severe pain. Stop if pain intensifies. This is a skill for chronic, stable sensation.

title: The Screen and the Movie
description: Recognize awareness as the screen on which the movie of experience plays.
short_description: Recognize awareness as the screen on which the movie of expe

content.objective: Recognize awareness as the screen on which the movie of experience plays.
instructions: Close your eyes and let thoughts, images, and sensations play.
Imagine them as a movie projected on a screen.
The movie changes constantly; the screen never does.
Notice: you are not the movie. You are not even the projector. You are the screen.
Rest as the unchanged space in which everything appears.

session_steps.title: Movie
session_steps.content: Let the mind's content play without interference.

session_steps.title: Screen
session_steps.content: Shift attention from the images to the space holding them.

session_steps.title: Unchanged
session_steps.content: Notice the screen is untouched by every scene.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest as the screen.

content.expected_experience: A vivid sense of being the unchanging context of experience rather than its content — often described as deeply restful.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. The metaphor is a pointer; if it becomes a distraction, return to simple breath watching.

title: Witnessing into Sleep
description: Carry a thread of witnessing awareness into the threshold of sleep.
short_description: Carry a thread of witnessing awareness into the threshold of

content.objective: Carry a thread of witnessing awareness into the threshold of sleep.
instructions: Lie down in your sleeping position.
Let the body relax completely — you are not trying to stay alert.
Keep a faint awareness of the process of falling asleep.
Watch the fading of thought without following any thought.
If you fall asleep, that is fine — the practice seeds recognition.

session_steps.title: Lie Down
session_steps.content: Settle into sleep posture. Release all effort.

session_steps.title: Relax
session_steps.content: Let the body sink. No alertness is forced.

session_steps.title: Faint Thread
session_steps.content: Keep a whisper of awareness on the threshold.

session_steps.title: Release
session_steps.content: Sleep is allowed. The seed is planted.

content.expected_experience: Sleep is sometimes experienced as a conscious transition. Even without lucidity, dreamless rest feels more restorative.
content.safety_notes: Do not fight sleep. This practice is the opposite of insomnia struggle — it invites surrender with a thread of awareness.

title: The Unchanging Witness
description: Notice what has never changed across your entire life — the witnessing itself.
short_description: Notice what has never changed across your entire life — the

content.objective: Notice what has never changed across your entire life — the witnessing itself.
instructions: Recall a childhood memory — see it, hear it, feel it.
Notice: the one remembering is the same one who experienced it.
Recall yesterday, today. The body changed, the thoughts changed.
Ask: what remained constant through every change?
Rest as the unchanged one.

session_steps.title: Childhood
session_steps.content: Recall an early memory vividly.

session_steps.title: Same One
session_steps.content: The witness of the memory is the witness now.

session_steps.title: Changes
session_steps.content: List what has changed — body, mind, circumstances.

session_steps.title: Constant
session_steps.content: Rest as what never changed.

content.expected_experience: A quiet recognition of continuity beneath change — the 'I' that is not any particular age, role, or story.
content.safety_notes: If childhood recall brings distress, choose a neutral memory or stop. This is recognition, not regression therapy.

title: Witness in Action
description: Maintain the witness while engaged in ordinary activity.
short_description: Maintain the witness while engaged in ordinary activity.

content.objective: Maintain the witness while engaged in ordinary activity.
instructions: Choose a simple activity: washing dishes, walking, typing.
Perform it at normal speed.
Keep a background awareness: 'I am the one doing this, and I am watching the one doing this.'
Notice the doer and the watcher coexisting.
When absorbed, gently re-include the witness without stopping the activity.

session_steps.title: Choose
session_steps.content: Pick an ordinary task.

session_steps.title: Do
session_steps.content: Perform the task normally.

session_steps.title: Double Awareness
session_steps.content: Act and watch the acting simultaneously.

session_steps.title: Notice
session_steps.content: The doer is an object too, seen by the witness.

content.expected_experience: Activity becomes lighter — full engagement plus freedom from being consumed by it. This is karma yoga's doorway.
content.safety_notes: Do not practice while driving or operating machinery until the dual awareness is stable. Safety first.

title: Witnessing Pleasure
description: Watch pleasant experience without grasping — the other half of equanimity.
short_description: Watch pleasant experience without grasping — the other half

content.objective: Watch pleasant experience without grasping — the other half of equanimity.
instructions: Bring to mind a genuine pleasure — warmth, taste, affection, beauty.
Feel it fully. Do not dampen it.
Notice the mind's impulse to hold on, repeat, secure it.
Watch the grasping impulse as an object.
Let the pleasure be enjoyed by the body-mind, while you remain the witness.

session_steps.title: Recall
session_steps.content: Bring a real pleasure to mind or senses.

session_steps.title: Enjoy
session_steps.content: Let it be fully felt — no suppression.

session_steps.title: Grasping
session_steps.content: Notice the impulse to hold on.

session_steps.title: Free Enjoyment
session_steps.content: Enjoyment without the grip — pleasure witnessed, not clung.

content.expected_experience: Pleasure deepens when not clutched. Enjoyment without dependency is discovered to be possible — and more sustainable.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. This practice balances the common tendency to only watch pain — joy deserves the same witness.

title: Natural Breath Observation
description: Feel the breath exactly as it is, before ever trying to change it.
short_description: Feel the breath exactly as it is, before ever trying to chan

content.objective: Feel the breath exactly as it is, before ever trying to change it.
instructions: Sit comfortably. Let the breath be entirely natural.
Find where the breath is most vivid: nostrils, chest, or belly.
Rest attention there. Do not adjust anything.
Notice the breath's texture: depth, rhythm, temperature, pauses.
When the mind wanders, the return is the practice.

session_steps.title: Find
session_steps.content: Locate the breath's most vivid point.

session_steps.title: Feel
session_steps.content: Feel the breath as it is — no correction.

session_steps.title: Texture
session_steps.content: Notice rhythm, temperature, pauses.

session_steps.title: Return
session_steps.content: Each return from wandering is one repetition.

content.expected_experience: The breath is discovered to be already intelligent — it regulates itself. Watching it settles the nervous system without effort.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Never force depth or length. Natural means natural.

title: Nostril Touch Awareness
description: Sharpen attention on the subtle sensations at the nostrils.
short_description: Sharpen attention on the subtle sensations at the nostrils.

content.objective: Sharpen attention on the subtle sensations at the nostrils.
instructions: Sit erect. Close your eyes.
Direct attention to the rim of the nostrils.
Feel the cool touch of air entering, the warmth of air leaving.
Stay with this small patch of skin like a sentinel.
When attention drifts, bring it back to the touch.

session_steps.title: Aim
session_steps.content: Point attention at the nostril rim.

session_steps.title: Cool and Warm
session_steps.content: Feel the temperature difference of in and out breath.

session_steps.title: Sentinel
session_steps.content: Hold attention on this small area.

session_steps.title: Return
session_steps.content: Each return strengthens the attention muscle.

content.expected_experience: A subtle, almost electric sensitivity develops at the nostrils — the classic anchor of anapanasati.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If nasal congestion blocks sensation, use the belly as the anchor instead.

title: Breath Counting to Ten
description: Stabilize wandering attention with the simple discipline of counting.
short_description: Stabilize wandering attention with the simple discipline of

content.objective: Stabilize wandering attention with the simple discipline of counting.
instructions: Sit comfortably. Let the breath flow naturally.
Count each exhale: one, two, three... up to ten.
At ten, return to one.
If you lose count — even at nine — return to one without self-criticism.
The losing and returning is where the training happens.

session_steps.title: Begin
session_steps.content: Start counting exhales from one.

session_steps.title: Count
session_steps.content: One through ten, then cycle back.

session_steps.title: Reset
session_steps.content: Any loss of count resets to one — gently.

session_steps.title: Notice
session_steps.content: Notice what steals the count. That is the mind's habit map.

content.expected_experience: Counting reveals the mind's wanderings with precision. Reaching ten without interruption feels like a small miracle.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If counting creates tension, drop the numbers and simply follow the breath.

title: Breath Counting to Ten — For Anxiety
description: Stabilize wandering attention with the simple discipline of counting.
short_description: Stabilize wandering attention with the simple discipline of

content.objective: Stabilize wandering attention with the simple discipline of counting. (For Anxiety variation.)

title: The Breath's Touchpoints
description: Map the breath's pathway through the body with fine attention.
short_description: Map the breath's pathway through the body with fine attentio

content.objective: Map the breath's pathway through the body with fine attention.
instructions: Follow one full breath from beginning to end.
Feel the air at the nostrils, then the throat, then the chest.
Feel the belly expand and release.
Trace the whole pathway as a continuous gesture.
Notice which touchpoint is most vivid today.

session_steps.title: One Breath
session_steps.content: Follow a single breath completely.

session_steps.title: Pathway
session_steps.content: Nostrils, throat, chest, belly — in sequence.

session_steps.title: Continuous
session_steps.content: Experience the breath as one unbroken movement.

session_steps.title: Vivid Point
session_steps.content: Which touchpoint speaks loudest today?

content.expected_experience: The breath becomes a felt journey rather than an abstraction. Body literacy improves with every session.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Breath Temperature
description: Discriminate subtle thermal qualities of the breath.
short_description: Discriminate subtle thermal qualities of the breath.

content.objective: Discriminate subtle thermal qualities of the breath.
instructions: Breathe naturally through the nose.
Feel the coolness of the incoming air at the nostrils.
Feel the warmth of the outgoing air.
Let this cool-warm rhythm become a gentle mantra of sensation.
Notice how attention on temperature slows the mind.

session_steps.title: Cool
session_steps.content: Feel the in-breath's cool touch.

session_steps.title: Warm
session_steps.content: Feel the out-breath's warmth.

session_steps.title: Rhythm
session_steps.content: Cool-warm, cool-warm — a sensory anchor.

session_steps.title: Settle
session_steps.content: Notice the mind quiet around sensation.

content.expected_experience: Fine sensory discrimination grows. The breath becomes a constant, elegant anchor available in any moment.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Breath Sound Listening
description: Use the faint sound of breathing as the object of attention.
short_description: Use the faint sound of breathing as the object of attention.

content.objective: Use the faint sound of breathing as the object of attention.
instructions: Sit quietly. Let the breath be natural.
Listen to the faint sound of air moving.
It may sound like a distant ocean or a whisper.
Rest attention on this subtle sound.
When sound and silence both are heard, rest in that.

session_steps.title: Listen
session_steps.content: Attend to the breath's faint sound.

session_steps.title: Ocean
session_steps.content: Let the sound fill awareness like distant surf.

session_steps.title: Silence
session_steps.content: Notice the silence between breath sounds.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest in sound and silence together.

content.expected_experience: The ordinary breath reveals itself as a soundscape. Attention becomes effortlessly absorbed.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Pause Awareness
description: Notice the natural pauses at the top and bottom of the breath.
short_description: Notice the natural pauses at the top and bottom of the breat

content.objective: Notice the natural pauses at the top and bottom of the breath.
instructions: Breathe naturally. Do not hold anything.
Notice the tiny pause after each inhale.
Notice the tiny pause after each exhale.
Rest in these spontaneous still points.
The pauses are windows — awareness naturally brightens there.

session_steps.title: Natural
session_steps.content: Let the breath be entirely unforced.

session_steps.title: Top Pause
session_steps.content: Notice the stillness after the inhale.

session_steps.title: Bottom Pause
session_steps.content: Notice the stillness after the exhale.

session_steps.title: Windows
session_steps.content: Rest in the pauses without creating them.

content.expected_experience: The breath's natural gaps become doorways to stillness. Retention happens on its own — never forced.
content.safety_notes: Never hold the breath deliberately in this practice. Only naturally occurring pauses are observed.

title: Breath and Emotion Link
description: Observe how emotion and breath shape each other in real time.
short_description: Observe how emotion and breath shape each other in real time

content.objective: Observe how emotion and breath shape each other in real time.
instructions: Sit quietly and notice the current emotional tone.
Feel how that tone lives in the breath — shallow, held, sighing, smooth.
Without changing anything, watch the link.
Let the breath be the window into the emotional state.
Notice: change the breath's pattern, and the emotion shifts — and vice versa.

session_steps.title: Tone
session_steps.content: Identify the present emotional weather.

session_steps.title: Breath Shape
session_steps.content: Feel the emotion's signature in the breath.

session_steps.title: Link
session_steps.content: Watch the two move together.

session_steps.title: Insight
session_steps.content: The breath is emotion's visible edge.

content.expected_experience: Emotion stops being invisible. The breath gives it a shape you can see, feel, and wisely influence.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. For overwhelming emotion, keep the session short and ground in the body afterwards.

title: Full-Body Breath
description: Experience the breath as a whole-body event, not just a lung event.
short_description: Experience the breath as a whole-body event, not just a lung

content.objective: Experience the breath as a whole-body event, not just a lung event.
instructions: Sit or lie down. Let the breath be natural.
Feel the breath in the belly, the ribs, the chest.
Feel the subtle movement of the spine, the shoulders, the throat.
Feel the whole body breathing — cells participating.
Rest as a breathing organism, not a body with a breath.

session_steps.title: Belly
session_steps.content: Feel the belly's movement.

session_steps.title: Ribs and Chest
session_steps.content: Feel the ribcage and chest.

session_steps.title: Whole
session_steps.content: Include spine, shoulders, throat — the whole organism.

session_steps.title: Organism
session_steps.content: Rest as a breathing being.

content.expected_experience: Breathing becomes a full-body tide. The sense of being a breathing organism — not a torso with lungs — is restorative.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Lie down if seated posture is uncomfortable.

title: Walking Breath Awareness
description: Synchronize attention with breath and step while moving.
short_description: Synchronize attention with breath and step while moving.

content.objective: Synchronize attention with breath and step while moving.
instructions: Walk at a slow, natural pace.
Feel the foot contact: heel, sole, toe.
Let the breath find its own rhythm with the steps.
When mind and step and breath align, stay there.
When they separate, notice the separation — that is the practice.

session_steps.title: Walk
session_steps.content: Begin walking slowly.

session_steps.title: Feet
session_steps.content: Feel each footfall.

session_steps.title: Align
session_steps.content: Let breath and steps find rhythm.

session_steps.title: Notice
session_steps.content: Watch alignment and misalignment.

content.expected_experience: Walking stops being transportation and becomes practice. Attention distributes across body, breath, and movement.
content.safety_notes: Walk on safe ground. Keep eyes open and aware of surroundings — this is not a trance exercise.

title: Three-Part Breath
description: Restore the full architecture of breathing — belly, ribs, chest — lost to chronic shallow breathing.
short_description: Restore the full architecture of breathing — belly, ribs, ch

content.objective: Restore the full architecture of breathing — belly, ribs, chest — lost to chronic shallow breathing.
instructions: Sit or lie down with one hand on the belly, one on the chest.
Inhale: fill the belly first, then widen the ribs, then lift the chest.
Exhale: release chest, ribs, belly — in reverse order.
Smooth the breath like a wave, not a pump.
Let each round be slower than the last.

session_steps.title: Hands
session_steps.content: Place hands on belly and chest. Feel the current breathing pattern.

session_steps.title: Wave In
session_steps.content: Belly, ribs, chest — one continuous inhale.

session_steps.title: Wave Out
session_steps.content: Chest, ribs, belly — one continuous exhale.

session_steps.title: Settle
session_steps.content: Let rounds become slower and smoother.

content.expected_experience: The breath becomes a full tidal wave. Many feel immediate calm as the nervous system reads 'safe'.
content.safety_notes: Never strain for depth. Smoothness over volume. Dizziness means you are forcing — return to natural breath.

title: Equal Breath
description: Balance the nervous system by matching inhale and exhale count for count.
short_description: Balance the nervous system by matching inhale and exhale cou

content.objective: Balance the nervous system by matching inhale and exhale count for count.
instructions: Breathe naturally through the nose.
Count the inhale: typically 3-5 counts.
Match the exhale to the same count.
Keep the counts equal — symmetry is the practice.
When the mind wanders, the count brings it back.

session_steps.title: Find Count
session_steps.content: Discover your natural inhale count.

session_steps.title: Match
session_steps.content: Set the exhale to the same count.

session_steps.title: Symmetry
session_steps.content: Maintain equal in and out for the full session.

session_steps.title: Settle
session_steps.content: Notice the balancing effect.

content.expected_experience: Symmetry in the breath produces symmetry in the mind — a classic prelude to deeper meditation.
content.safety_notes: Keep counts comfortable (3-6). Forced counting creates tension — the opposite of the goal.

title: Box Breathing
description: Build stress resilience through four equal phases: in, hold, out, hold.
short_description: Build stress resilience through four equal phases: in, hold,

content.objective: Build stress resilience through four equal phases: in, hold, out, hold.
instructions: Exhale fully to begin.
Inhale through the nose for 4 counts.
Hold gently for 4 counts — no strain.
Exhale slowly for 4 counts.
Hold empty for 4 counts. That is one round. Repeat.

session_steps.title: Empty
session_steps.content: Exhale fully to start the cycle.

session_steps.title: Four Phases
session_steps.content: In 4 · Hold 4 · Out 4 · Hold 4.

session_steps.title: Rounds
session_steps.content: Complete steady rounds without force.

session_steps.title: Notice
session_steps.content: Feel the regulation of the nervous system.

content.expected_experience: Used by athletes and first responders, box breathing rapidly downshifts arousal. The box becomes a portable anchor.
content.safety_notes: Holds must never feel strained. If holding creates tension, practice without retention — equal inhale and exhale still works.

title: 4-7-8 Relaxing Breath
description: Activate the parasympathetic response with a long, structured exhale.
short_description: Activate the parasympathetic response with a long, structure

content.objective: Activate the parasympathetic response with a long, structured exhale.
instructions: Place the tongue behind the upper front teeth.
Exhale completely through the mouth with a soft whoosh.
Inhale quietly through the nose for 4 counts.
Hold for 7 counts.
Exhale through the mouth for 8 counts. Repeat for 4 rounds.

session_steps.title: Tongue
session_steps.content: Rest tongue behind upper front teeth.

session_steps.title: Whoosh Out
session_steps.content: Exhale fully with an audible release.
In 4, hold 7, out 8 — one round.

session_steps.title: Four Rounds
session_steps.content: Complete four rounds, then breathe naturally.

content.expected_experience: A natural tranquilizer. Many use it before sleep or difficult conversations. The long exhale is the active ingredient.
content.safety_notes: The hold is optional — in 4, out 8 still works. Never force. Sit or lie down; lightheadedness means stop and breathe normally.

In 4, hold 7, out 8 — one round.

session_steps.title: Four Rounds
session_steps.content: Complete four rounds, then breathe naturally.

content.expected_experience: A natural tranquilizer. Many use it before sleep or difficult conversations. The long exhale is the active ingredient.
content.safety_notes: The hold is optional — in 4, out 8 still works. Never force. Sit or lie down; lightheadedness means stop and breathe normally.

title: Alternate Nostril Breathing
description: Balance the left and right energy channels — the classic nadi shodhana.
short_description: Balance the left and right energy channels — the classic nad

content.objective: Balance the left and right energy channels — the classic nadi shodhana.
instructions: Sit erect. Rest the left hand on the knee.
Right thumb closes the right nostril; inhale left.
Close the left nostril with the ring finger; open and exhale right.
Inhale right, close, exhale left. That is one round.
Keep the breath slow, quiet, and unforced.

session_steps.title: Setup
session_steps.content: Nassagra mudra — thumb and ring finger govern the nostrils.

session_steps.title: Round
session_steps.content: In left, out right, in right, out left.

session_steps.title: Steady
session_steps.content: Keep rounds slow, quiet, even.

session_steps.title: Finish
session_steps.content: End with a natural breath. Notice the balance.

content.expected_experience: A profound balancing effect — many report a quiet, centered clarity within minutes. The classic preparation for meditation.
contraindications: severe nasal congestion — wait or use breath awareness instead
content.safety_notes: No retention for beginners. Just the alternating flow. If one nostril is blocked, breathe through the open one without force.

title: Ocean Breath
description: Create the oceanic sound of ujjayi to anchor attention and build inner heat gently.
short_description: Create the oceanic sound of ujjayi to anchor attention and b

content.objective: Create the oceanic sound of ujjayi to anchor attention and build inner heat gently.
instructions: Inhale through the nose, slightly constricting the back of the throat.
Produce a soft oceanic sound — like a distant wave.
Keep the same gentle constriction on the exhale.
Let the sound become the object of meditation.
The breath should be audible to you, not to someone across the room.

session_steps.title: Sound
session_steps.content: Find the throat constriction that makes the ocean sound.

session_steps.title: In and Out
session_steps.content: Maintain the sound on both sides of the breath.

session_steps.title: Anchor
session_steps.content: Let the sound hold attention.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest in the rhythm of the waves.

content.expected_experience: The breath becomes a private soundtrack. Attention locks onto the sound effortlessly — ujjayi is meditation's training wheels and teacher.
content.safety_notes: The constriction is gentle, at the throat — never force the lungs. If the voice tires, the constriction is too strong.

title: Gentle Bellows
description: Energize with active, rhythmic breathing — bhastrika at a safe, moderate pace.
short_description: Energize with active, rhythmic breathing — bhastrika at a sa

content.objective: Energize with active, rhythmic breathing — bhastrika at a safe, moderate pace.
instructions: Sit erect with a tall spine.
Inhale and exhale actively through the nose — the belly pumps like a bellows.
Keep the pace moderate: about one breath per second.
Do 10 breaths, then rest with a slow natural breath.
Repeat for 3 rounds. Stop if any dizziness appears.

session_steps.title: Posture
session_steps.content: Spine tall, shoulders relaxed.

session_steps.title: Pump
session_steps.content: Active in-and-out, belly moving — 10 breaths.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: One slow natural breath.

session_steps.title: Rounds
session_steps.content: Three rounds total, then sit in stillness.

content.expected_experience: A clean, alert energy — like opening a window. The pause after each round often feels spacious and clear.
contraindications: anxiety disorders (can trigger panic in some)
content.safety_notes: Moderate pace only — this is not hyperventilation. Stop immediately on dizziness. Practice seated, never standing initially. Not before sleep.

title: Skull-Shining Breath
description: Kapalabhati — cleansing, clarifying bursts of exhalation with passive inhalation.
short_description: Kapalabhati — cleansing, clarifying bursts of exhalation wit

content.objective: Kapalabhati — cleansing, clarifying bursts of exhalation with passive inhalation.
instructions: Sit erect. Take a deep inhale.
Exhale sharply through the nose by contracting the lower belly.
Let the inhale happen passively — the focus is on the exhale.
Pump 20 exhalations at a steady rhythm.
End with a slow exhale, then a natural breath. Three rounds total.

session_steps.title: Inhale
session_steps.content: One deep breath to begin.

session_steps.title: Pump
session_steps.content: 20 sharp passive-exhale pumps, belly-led.

session_steps.title: Release
session_steps.content: Slow exhale, natural breath, pause.

session_steps.title: Three Rounds
session_steps.content: Build from 20 to 30 pumps across rounds as comfort allows.

content.expected_experience: A clarifying, scrubbing energy — the skull feels 'shined'. Alertness rises without caffeine's jitter.
content.safety_notes: Sharp but not violent. The exhale is active, the inhale passive. Stop on any dizziness, headache, or anxiety. Never practice kapalabhati lying down or in water.

title: Cooling Breath
description: Sheetali — draw air over the tongue's curl to cool the system and calm the mind.
short_description: Sheetali — draw air over the tongue's curl to cool the syste

content.objective: Sheetali — draw air over the tongue's curl to cool the system and calm the mind.
instructions: Curl the tongue into a tube (or, if unable, part the lips slightly and place the tongue behind the teeth).
Inhale slowly through the curled tongue — feel the coolness.
Close the mouth, exhale through the nose.
Keep rounds slow and even.
Notice the cooling quality spreading through the chest.

session_steps.title: Tongue
session_steps.content: Curl the tongue or position it behind the teeth.

session_steps.title: Cool In
session_steps.content: Inhale through the curled tongue — taste the coolness.

session_steps.title: Close and Out
session_steps.content: Close mouth, exhale through nose.

session_steps.title: Cooling
session_steps.content: Feel the cooling spread. Rest in it.

content.expected_experience: A literal cooling of the body-mind — traditionally used for heat, anger, and inflamed states. The mind follows the body's temperature down.
content.safety_notes: If the tongue cannot curl, use sheetkari (teeth slightly parted, tongue flat). Both are safe and gentle.

title: Humming Bee Breath
description: Bhramari — the humming exhale that soothes the vagus nerve and quiets mental noise.
short_description: Bhramari — the humming exhale that soothes the vagus nerve a

content.objective: Bhramari — the humming exhale that soothes the vagus nerve and quiets mental noise.
instructions: Sit erect. Close the ears gently with the thumbs, index fingers on the eyes.
Inhale deeply through the nose.
Exhale with a steady humming sound — like a bee — mouth closed.
Feel the vibration in the skull, face, and chest.
Keep the hum even and unhurried. Six to ten rounds.

session_steps.title: Close
session_steps.content: Thumbs close the ears; fingers rest on the eyes.

session_steps.title: Inhale
session_steps.content: Deep inhale through the nose.

session_steps.title: Hum
session_steps.content: Long humming exhale — feel the vibration.

session_steps.title: Resonance
session_steps.content: Rest in the residual vibration between rounds.

content.expected_experience: The hum vibrates through the head like a resonance chamber. Mental chatter often stops mid-hum — one of the fastest calming techniques.
contraindications: severe anxiety about breath retention (keep it simple)
content.safety_notes: The hum should be comfortable, not loud. If closing the ears feels claustrophobic, simply hum with open ears — the vibration still works.

title: Candle Gazing
description: Develop one-pointed concentration through steady visual fixation — classical trataka.
short_description: Develop one-pointed concentration through steady visual fixa

content.objective: Develop one-pointed concentration through steady visual fixation — classical trataka.
instructions: Place a candle at eye level, an arm's length away, in a dim room.
Gaze at the flame without blinking, eyes relaxed.
When the eyes water or tire, close them.
Hold the afterimage of the flame at the eyebrow center.
When the afterimage fades, open the eyes and repeat.

session_steps.title: Set
session_steps.content: Candle at eye level, arm's length, steady flame.

session_steps.title: Gaze
session_steps.content: Soft, unblinking focus on the flame.

session_steps.title: Close
session_steps.content: Close eyes; hold the afterimage at the brow.

session_steps.title: Repeat
session_steps.content: Open when the image fades. Three cycles.

content.expected_experience: Attention becomes laser-like. The afterimage phase often feels luminous and deeply quiet — a direct taste of dharana.
content.safety_notes: Never gaze at the sun. Use a steady candle flame, not a lamp with a moving wick. Stop if eyes strain.

title: Counting to One Hundred
description: Extend concentration span by counting breaths to one hundred without losing the thread.
short_description: Extend concentration span by counting breaths to one hundred

content.objective: Extend concentration span by counting breaths to one hundred without losing the thread.
instructions: Sit erect. Breathe naturally.
Count each exhale: 1, 2, 3... continuing to 100.
If you lose the number, return to 1 — no frustration.
Keep the counting soft, like a background hum.
Reaching 100 without interruption is the milestone.

session_steps.title: Begin
session_steps.content: Start counting exhales from one.

session_steps.title: Sustain
session_steps.content: Count steadily toward one hundred.

session_steps.title: Reset
session_steps.content: Any loss returns to one — the reset is part of the training.

session_steps.title: Milestone
session_steps.content: Notice the state of mind when counting flows unbroken.

content.expected_experience: A long unbroken count reveals how attention actually behaves — and trains it like a muscle with visible results.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If counting becomes obsessive, drop to counting to ten and back.

title: The Bindu Dot
description: Fix attention on a single visual point until the mind stops wandering.
short_description: Fix attention on a single visual point until the mind stops

content.objective: Fix attention on a single visual point until the mind stops wandering.
instructions: Draw or place a small dot at eye level on a plain wall.
Sit at a comfortable distance. Soften the gaze.
Rest attention on the dot — nothing else exists.
When thoughts pull, the dot gently retrieves you.
Notice the dot becoming brighter, larger, alive with attention.

session_steps.title: Place
session_steps.content: A small dot, eye level, plain background.

session_steps.title: Fix
session_steps.content: Soft, steady gaze on the dot.

session_steps.title: Retrieve
session_steps.content: Each return to the dot is one repetition.

session_steps.title: Brighten
session_steps.content: Notice the dot's apparent luminosity grow.

content.expected_experience: The dot becomes a gravity well for attention. Concentration stops being effortful and becomes absorption.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Blink naturally; do not stare to the point of strain.

title: Sound Anchor Focus
description: Use a continuous external sound as the single point of attention.
short_description: Use a continuous external sound as the single point of atten

content.objective: Use a continuous external sound as the single point of attention.
instructions: Choose a steady sound: a ticking clock, a fan, distant traffic, a singing bowl.
Close your eyes and locate the sound.
Rest all attention on the sound's texture.
When the mind comments, return to the sound itself.
Notice the space between the sound and the hearer.

session_steps.title: Choose
session_steps.content: Select one steady sound in the environment.

session_steps.title: Locate
session_steps.content: Find the sound with full attention.

session_steps.title: Texture
session_steps.content: Explore the sound's qualities — pitch, rhythm, edge.

session_steps.title: Space
session_steps.content: Notice the hearer behind the hearing.

content.expected_experience: Sound proves to be an excellent anchor — continuous, effortless, and revealing of the mind's wanderings.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Choose moderate volume — this is attention training, not endurance.

title: Image Hold
description: Hold a simple visual image in the mind's eye without distortion.
short_description: Hold a simple visual image in the mind's eye without distort

content.objective: Hold a simple visual image in the mind's eye without distortion.
instructions: Look at a simple image — a flower, a symbol, a geometric shape — for one minute.
Close your eyes and recreate it internally.
When the image fades or distorts, open your eyes and look again.
Repeat until the internal image holds steady.
The stability of the image reflects the stability of attention.

session_steps.title: Look
session_steps.content: Study a simple image for one minute.

session_steps.title: Recreate
session_steps.content: Close eyes; rebuild the image internally.

session_steps.title: Refresh
session_steps.content: Faded? Look again, then close.

session_steps.title: Steady
session_steps.content: Hold the image unbroken for as long as possible.

content.expected_experience: The mind's eye strengthens measurably. A held image becomes a portable object of meditation anywhere.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If visualizing is difficult, use a real object with eyes open — equally valid.

instructions: Look at a simple image — a flower, a symbol, a geometric shape — for one minute.
Close your eyes and recreate it internally.
When the image fades or distorts, open your eyes and look again.
Repeat until the internal image holds steady.
The stability of the image reflects the stability of attention.

session_steps.title: Look
session_steps.content: Study a simple image for one minute.

session_steps.title: Recreate
session_steps.content: Close eyes; rebuild the image internally.

session_steps.title: Refresh
session_steps.content: Faded? Look again, then close.

session_steps.title: Steady
session_steps.content: Hold the image unbroken for as long as possible.

content.expected_experience: The mind's eye strengthens measurably. A held image becomes a portable object of meditation anywhere.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If visualizing is difficult, use a real object with eyes open — equally valid.

title: Mid-Spine Point
description: Focus attention on the body's central axis — a subtle, always-available anchor.
short_description: Focus attention on the body's central axis — a subtle, alway

content.objective: Focus attention on the body's central axis — a subtle, always-available anchor.
instructions: Sit erect. Feel the spine as a central column.
Place attention at the mid-spine, behind the heart, inside the body.
Rest there like a finger resting on a point in space.
When attention slides, slide it back — gently, endlessly.
Notice how this inner point steadies the whole posture.

session_steps.title: Column
session_steps.content: Feel the spine as the body's axis.

session_steps.title: Point
session_steps.content: Rest attention at the mid-spine, behind the heart.

session_steps.title: Return
session_steps.content: Endless gentle returns — that is the practice.

session_steps.title: Steady
session_steps.content: Notice the steadying effect on body and mind.

content.expected_experience: An inner anchor that travels with you — no candle, no sound, no object needed. Concentration becomes embodied.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. The point is felt, not forced — subtle attention, not muscular effort.

title: Backward Counting
description: Challenge the mind's momentum by counting backwards — a concentration stress test.
short_description: Challenge the mind's momentum by counting backwards — a conc

content.objective: Challenge the mind's momentum by counting backwards — a concentration stress test.
instructions: Sit erect. Begin counting backwards from 100.
Count with each exhale: 100, 99, 98...
Any mistake means returning to 100.
Keep the numbers clean — no rushing.
Notice how the mind resists the reverse order.

session_steps.title: Start
session_steps.content: Begin at 100, counting down with each exhale.

session_steps.title: Descend
session_steps.content: Steady descent — 100 to 1.

session_steps.title: Reset
session_steps.content: Any slip returns to 100 without drama.

session_steps.title: Observe
session_steps.content: Watch the mind's resistance to reversal.

content.expected_experience: Backward counting exposes the mind's forward habits. The struggle itself is the training — and it transfers to daily focus.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If frustration rises, count down by tens (100, 90, 80) instead.

title: Word Saturation
description: Saturate the mind with a single word until its meaning dissolves into pure sound.
short_description: Saturate the mind with a single word until its meaning disso

content.objective: Saturate the mind with a single word until its meaning dissolves into pure sound.
instructions: Choose one word: peace, om, stillness, light.
Repeat it silently with each breath — in and out.
Let the word fill the entire mind.
Notice the moment the word stops meaning anything and becomes pure vibration.
Rest in that saturation.

session_steps.title: Choose
session_steps.content: One word, chosen simply.

session_steps.title: Repeat
session_steps.content: The word rides each breath.

session_steps.title: Saturate
session_steps.content: The word fills all mental space.

session_steps.title: Dissolve
session_steps.content: Meaning dissolves into sound. Rest there.

content.expected_experience: A word repeated enough stops being a word — it becomes a vibration that carries attention into quiet.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Choose a word with positive or neutral charge for you personally.

title: Grid Attention
description: Train distributed attention by holding a visual grid in awareness.
short_description: Train distributed attention by holding a visual grid in awar

content.objective: Train distributed attention by holding a visual grid in awareness.
instructions: Draw a simple 3×3 grid on paper or imagine one.
Place attention on the center cell.
Move attention to each cell in sequence — slowly, deliberately.
Then hold the whole grid in awareness at once.
Notice the difference between sequential and simultaneous attention.

session_steps.title: Grid
session_steps.content: A 3×3 grid, drawn or imagined.

session_steps.title: Sequence
session_steps.content: Move attention cell by cell.

session_steps.title: Whole

title: Mantra Precision
description: Refine concentration by repeating a mantra with exactness — every repetition identical.
short_description: Refine concentration by repeating a mantra with exactness —

content.objective: Refine concentration by repeating a mantra with exactness — every repetition identical.
instructions: Choose a short mantra: om, so ham, peace.
Repeat it silently, one repetition per breath.
Attend to exactness: same inner sound, same rhythm, same weight.
When a repetition is sloppy, notice without judgment — and refine the next.
Precision itself becomes the meditation.

session_steps.title: Choose
session_steps.content: One short mantra.

session_steps.title: Repeat
session_steps.content: One repetition per breath.

session_steps.title: Refine
session_steps.content: Attend to exactness in every repetition.

session_steps.title: Notice
session_steps.content: Precision reveals the mind's micro-habits.

content.expected_experience: Concentration sharpens to a fine point. The gap between repetitions becomes visible — and quietly expansive.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Flowing Awareness
description: Sustain unbroken attention on one object — the transition from concentration to meditation.
short_description: Sustain unbroken attention on one object — the transition fr

content.objective: Sustain unbroken attention on one object — the transition from concentration to meditation.
instructions: Begin with a dharana object: breath, sound, or dot.
Hold attention without the effort of holding.
Notice when attention becomes continuous — no gaps, no struggle.
The object and the watcher begin to feel like one movement.
Rest in the flow. This is dhyana's doorway.

session_steps.title: Anchor
session_steps.content: Choose one object and settle on it.

session_steps.title: Flow
session_steps.content: Attention becomes continuous — effort dissolves into flow.

session_steps.title: One Movement
session_steps.content: Watcher and watched merge into one gesture.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest in the flow without claiming it.

content.expected_experience: Meditation stops being something you do and becomes something that happens. Time perception often shifts.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Dhyana cannot be forced — if effort dominates, return to dharana. The flow arrives by permission, not will.

title: Absorption in Sound
description: Let attention dissolve into a sustained sound until listener and sound are one.
short_description: Let attention dissolve into a sustained sound until listener

content.objective: Let attention dissolve into a sustained sound until listener and sound are one.
instructions: Play a sustained tone: singing bowl, tanpura, or a steady environmental hum.
Listen with complete attention.
Notice the sound's beginning, middle, end — and the silence after.
Let attention merge with the sound.
When the sound ends, rest in the silence it leaves.

session_steps.title: Tone
session_steps.content: Begin a sustained tone.

session_steps.title: Listen
session_steps.content: Complete attention on the sound.

session_steps.title: Merge
session_steps.content: Attention dissolves into the sound.

session_steps.title: Silence
session_steps.content: Rest in the silence the sound leaves behind.

content.expected_experience: Sound becomes a vehicle out of the separate self. The silence after the tone is often experienced as vast.
content.safety_notes: Keep volume gentle. The practice is about attention, not loudness.

title: The Unbroken Thread
description: Maintain one thread of awareness across the entire session — no gaps allowed.
short_description: Maintain one thread of awareness across the entire session —

content.objective: Maintain one thread of awareness across the entire session — no gaps allowed.
instructions: Choose a simple object: the breath at the nostrils.
Commit: not one breath will pass unattended.
When attention breaks, note the gap — without guilt — and re-thread.
The goal is not perfection but the noticing of gaps.
Over sessions, the thread unbreaks.
