title: Meditation on Space
description: Use space itself — inner and outer — as the object of meditation.
short_description: Use space itself — inner and outer — as the object of medita

content.objective: Use space itself — inner and outer — as the object of meditation.
instructions: Sit quietly. Notice the space around your body.
Notice the space inside the room, the space between sounds.
Turn attention to the space inside the head — the room of awareness.
Rest as space: boundless, ungraspable, already everywhere.
Thoughts and sounds appear in space; space is unchanged.

session_steps.title: Outer Space
session_steps.content: Notice the space filling the room.

session_steps.title: Between
session_steps.content: Notice space between sounds, between thoughts.

session_steps.title: Inner Space
session_steps.content: The space inside the head — awareness's room.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest as space itself.

content.expected_experience: Space as an object is uniquely freeing — it cannot be grasped, so attention relaxes into it. Many glimpse non-dual awareness here.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If boundlessness triggers anxiety, narrow to the space of the room — concrete, contained.

title: Heart-Centered Absorption
description: Settle attention in the heart center and let warmth and clarity arise.
short_description: Settle attention in the heart center and let warmth and clar

content.objective: Settle attention in the heart center and let warmth and clarity arise.
instructions: Sit quietly. Bring attention to the center of the chest.
Feel the heart region — physically, then subtly.
Allow a natural warmth or openness to be there, if present.
Rest attention in the heart like a bird on a branch.
Whatever arises — emotion, image, stillness — let it be held by the heart's space.

session_steps.title: Chest
session_steps.content: Settle attention at the heart center.

session_steps.title: Feel
session_steps.content: Feel the region — physical and subtle.

session_steps.title: Warmth
session_steps.content: Allow whatever warmth or openness is present.

session_steps.title: Bird
session_steps.content: Rest like a bird on a branch — alert, unclenched.

content.expected_experience: The heart center is described in every tradition as the seat of the self. Attention resting there often brings unexpected tenderness and clarity.
content.safety_notes: If heart-centered attention triggers grief, that is information — allow it briefly, then ground in the feet. Seek support if it persists.

title: Meditation on the Infinite
description: Expand attention beyond boundaries — the classic 'infinite' meditation of the Upanishads.
short_description: Expand attention beyond boundaries — the classic 'infinite'

content.objective: Expand attention beyond boundaries — the classic 'infinite' meditation of the Upanishads.
instructions: Sit quietly and let the eyes close.
Begin with awareness of the body's boundaries.
Let attention expand past the skin, past the room, past the city.
Rest in the sense of boundlessness — without imagining anything specific.
The infinite is not a picture; it is the absence of edges.

session_steps.title: Boundary
session_steps.content: Feel the body's edges.

session_steps.title: Expand
session_steps.content: Attention moves past skin, room, city.

session_steps.title: Boundless
session_steps.content: Rest in boundlessness — no image, just no edges.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Remain as the boundless one.

content.expected_experience: A distinctive expansion — the usual container of self feels optional. Often followed by deep calm and a changed sense of scale.
contraindications: anxiety or depersonalization history — practice with eyes open, on a small object, instead
content.safety_notes: If expansion triggers fear, immediately contract attention to the feet or hands. Boundaried attention is always available as a refuge.

Let attention expand past the skin, past the room, past the city.
Rest in the sense of boundlessness — without imagining anything specific.
The infinite is not a picture; it is the absence of edges.

session_steps.title: Boundary
session_steps.content: Feel the body's edges.

session_steps.title: Expand
session_steps.content: Attention moves past skin, room, city.

session_steps.title: Boundless
session_steps.content: Rest in boundlessness — no image, just no edges.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Remain as the boundless one.

content.expected_experience: A distinctive expansion — the usual container of self feels optional. Often followed by deep calm and a changed sense of scale.
contraindications: anxiety or depersonalization history — practice with eyes open, on a small object, instead

title: One-Pointed Rest
description: The simplest dhyana: rest attention on one point until even the rester is forgotten.
short_description: The simplest dhyana: rest attention on one point until even

content.objective: The simplest dhyana: rest attention on one point until even the rester is forgotten.
instructions: Choose one point: breath at the nostrils, a dot, a sound.
Rest attention there with no agenda.
No striving, no achieving — just resting.
When even the intention to meditate is seen as an object, rest deeper.
This is meditation without meditation.

session_steps.title: Point
session_steps.content: Choose one anchor.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest attention — no agenda.

session_steps.title: Forget
session_steps.content: Even the meditator becomes an object seen.

session_steps.title: Deeper
session_steps.content: Rest without a rester.

content.expected_experience: Effortless attention — the hallmark of dhyana. It cannot be manufactured, only allowed. This practice is the allowing.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Sleepiness is fine — the practice continues in rest.

title: The Ocean of Awareness
description: Experience awareness as an ocean — waves of thought on an unmoving depth.
short_description: Experience awareness as an ocean — waves of thought on an un

content.objective: Experience awareness as an ocean — waves of thought on an unmoving depth.
instructions: Close your eyes. Let thoughts, feelings, and sensations arise.
Imagine them as waves on the surface of a vast ocean.
Let attention descend below the surface — into the still depth.
Waves continue; the depth is unmoved.
Rest in the depth. The surface takes care of itself.

session_steps.title: Waves
session_steps.content: Let mental content arise as waves.

session_steps.title: Descend
session_steps.content: Attention moves below the surface.

session_steps.title: Depth
session_steps.content: Rest in the unmoving depth.

session_steps.title: Surface
session_steps.content: Notice the surface from the depth.

content.expected_experience: The ocean metaphor gives a stable felt-sense of non-reactivity. Surface storms continue, but they no longer capsize the meditator.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If the depth feels like drowning, return to the surface — waves are welcome too.

title: Timeless Sitting
description: Drop the clock and sit until the sense of time dissolves.
short_description: Drop the clock and sit until the sense of time dissolves.

content.objective: Drop the clock and sit until the sense of time dissolves.
instructions: Set a gentle alarm for 20-30 minutes — then forget it.
Sit with no goal, no object, no improvement.
Let time become irrelevant. There is nothing to get to.
When the alarm sounds, notice: was there time at all?
The practice is the dissolution of the clock inside the head.

session_steps.title: Alarm
session_steps.content: Set a soft alarm. Then release all concern for time.

session_steps.title: No Goal
session_steps.content: Sit with nothing to achieve.

session_steps.title: Dissolve
session_steps.content: Let the inner clock dissolve.

session_steps.title: Return
session_steps.content: The alarm returns you. Notice what happened to time.

content.expected_experience: Time is discovered to be a mental construction. Sessions often feel shorter than they are — or strangely complete.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Use the alarm — surrendering to time does not mean ignoring commitments.

title: Meditation Without Object
description: Rest in awareness itself — no object, no anchor, no doing.
short_description: Rest in awareness itself — no object, no anchor, no doing.

content.objective: Rest in awareness itself — no object, no anchor, no doing.
instructions: Sit quietly. Let every object of attention go.
Not breath, not sound, not body — awareness itself.
Notice that awareness needs no object to exist.
Rest as the aware space in which objects appear.
This is the simplest and most radical meditation.

session_steps.title: Release
session_steps.content: Let go of every object.

session_steps.title: Awareness
session_steps.content: Rest in awareness itself.

session_steps.title: No Object Needed
session_steps.content: Notice awareness exists without anything to be aware of.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest as the aware space.

content.expected_experience: Objectless awareness is described across traditions as the natural state — not blank, but vividly, quietly awake. Even a glimpse reshapes practice.
contraindications: psychosis or severe dissociation — practice with an object instead
content.safety_notes: If objectless rest becomes unsettling, immediately return to the breath or body. Objects are not a crutch — they are a legitimate path.

content.objective: Rest in awareness itself — no object, no anchor, no doing. (For Anxiety variation.)
instructions: Sit quietly. Let every object of attention go.
Not breath, not sound, not body — awareness itself.
Notice that awareness needs no object to exist.
Rest as the aware space in which objects appear.
This is the simplest and most radical meditation.

session_steps.title: Release
session_steps.content: Let go of every object.

session_steps.title: Awareness
session_steps.content: Rest in awareness itself.

session_steps.title: No Object Needed
session_steps.content: Notice awareness exists without anything to be aware of.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest as the aware space.

content.expected_experience: Objectless awareness is described across traditions as the natural state — not blank, but vividly, quietly awake. Even a glimpse reshapes practice.
contraindications: psychosis or severe dissociation — practice with an object instead
content.safety_notes: If objectless rest becomes unsettling, immediately return to the breath or body. Objects are not a crutch — they are a legitimate path.

title: Classic Rotation of Consciousness
description: Systematically rotate awareness through every body part — the classical yoga nidra structure.
short_description: Systematically rotate awareness through every body part — th

content.objective: Systematically rotate awareness through every body part — the classical yoga nidra structure.
instructions: Lie down in savasana. Make any last adjustments.
The guide (or your memory) names each body part.
Move awareness to each part without moving the body.
Rotate: right thumb, index, middle, ring, little... up through the whole body.
The rotation itself induces the hypnagogic state yoga nidra is known for.

session_steps.title: Settle
session_steps.content: Lie still. Adjust once, then commit to stillness.

session_steps.title: Rotate
session_steps.content: Awareness travels part by part — right side, left side, trunk, face.

session_steps.title: Whole
session_steps.content: Feel the whole body as one field of sensation.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest in the awareness of the whole body.

content.expected_experience: The rotation reliably induces deep rest while awareness remains — the signature yoga nidra state between waking and sleep.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If you fall asleep, the practice still worked — set an intention to return if needed.

title: The River Visualization
description: Use a flowing river visualization to carry awareness into deep rest.
short_description: Use a flowing river visualization to carry awareness into de

content.objective: Use a flowing river visualization to carry awareness into deep rest.
instructions: Lie down and settle.
Imagine lying beside a slow, wide river.
Each thought is a leaf placed on the water.
Watch leaves float away without following them.
Let the river's sound become the only world.

session_steps.title: Riverbank
session_steps.content: Settle beside the imagined river.

session_steps.title: Leaves
session_steps.content: Place each thought on a leaf.

session_steps.title: Float
session_steps.content: Watch thoughts float away.

session_steps.title: Sound
session_steps.content: Let the river's sound hold you.

content.expected_experience: The river gives the mind a job it accepts — carrying thoughts away. Deep rest follows quickly.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Opposite Sensations
description: Use pairs of opposite sensations — heavy/light, hot/cold — to deepen body awareness.
short_description: Use pairs of opposite sensations — heavy/light, hot/cold — t

content.objective: Use pairs of opposite sensations — heavy/light, hot/cold — to deepen body awareness.
instructions: Lie down and settle.
Feel the body as heavy — sinking into the floor.
Then feel the body as light — floating, weightless.
Alternate: heavy, light, heavy, light.
Notice the body becomes a field of pure sensation, free of identity.

session_steps.title: Heavy
session_steps.content: Feel the body sink — heavy, grounded.

session_steps.title: Light
session_steps.content: Feel the body float — light, weightless.

session_steps.title: Alternate
session_steps.content: Heavy, light, heavy, light — the pendulum swings.

session_steps.title: Field
session_steps.content: Rest as pure sensation.

content.expected_experience: Opposites reveal the body as sensation rather than 'me'. This is the classical yoga nidra technique for dissolving identification.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Sankalpa Setting
description: Plant a resolve (sankalpa) in the fertile soil of the hypnagogic state.
short_description: Plant a resolve (sankalpa) in the fertile soil of the hypnag

content.objective: Plant a resolve (sankalpa) in the fertile soil of the hypnagogic state.
instructions: Lie down and settle into yoga nidra's edge of sleep.
Formulate your resolve in one short, positive, present-tense sentence.
Repeat it silently three times — slowly, with feeling.
Let it sink below the thinking mind.
The sankalpa works on the deep soil where habits grow.

session_steps.title: Edge
session_steps.content: Reach the drowsy, wakeful edge.

title: Nidra for Anxiety
description: A targeted yoga nidra sequence for anxious nervous systems.
short_description: A targeted yoga nidra sequence for anxious nervous systems.

content.objective: A targeted yoga nidra sequence for anxious nervous systems.
instructions: Lie down. Feel the anxiety without trying to fix it.
Rotate awareness slowly through the body — extra time on the belly and chest.
Feel the breath's natural pause after each exhale.
Visualize a safe, quiet place — real or imagined.
End with the sankalpa: 'I am safe in this moment.'

session_steps.title: Acknowledge
session_steps.content: Feel the anxiety as present, not as enemy.

session_steps.title: Rotate
session_steps.content: Slow body rotation — belly and chest get extra attention.

session_steps.title: Pause
session_steps.content: Feel the natural pause after exhale.

session_steps.title: Safe Place
session_steps.content: Visualize safety. Sankalpa: 'I am safe in this moment.'

content.expected_experience: Anxiety is met, not fought. The body learns — in the hypnagogic state — that rest is possible again.
contraindications: acute panic — use only after the peak has passed
content.safety_notes: For acute panic, use shorter grounding practices first. Nidra meets anxiety best when it has already begun to settle.

title: Nidra for Sleep
description: The sleep-entry sequence — yoga nidra designed to be abandoned mid-way to sleep.
short_description: The sleep-entry sequence — yoga nidra designed to be abandon

content.objective: The sleep-entry sequence — yoga nidra designed to be abandoned mid-way to sleep.
instructions: Lie in bed, lights off.
Rotate awareness through the body — slowly, drowsily.
Let the rotation become indistinct. Sleep is allowed to arrive.
If you reach the end, repeat the rotation.
There is no failure here — sleep is the success condition.

session_steps.title: Bed
session_steps.content: Lie down in sleeping position.

session_steps.title: Rotate
session_steps.content: Slow, drowsy body rotation.

session_steps.title: Blur
session_steps.content: Let the rotation blur. Sleep may arrive.

session_steps.title: Success
session_steps.content: Falling asleep mid-practice is the goal.

content.expected_experience: The most reliable non-pharmacological sleep entry many practitioners report. The rotation occupies the mind just enough to let sleep through.
content.safety_notes: Do not practice while driving or operating machinery. This practice's purpose is sleep.

title: Chakra Rotation in Nidra
description: Rotate awareness through the seven energy centers in deep rest.
short_description: Rotate awareness through the seven energy centers in deep re

content.objective: Rotate awareness through the seven energy centers in deep rest.
instructions: Lie down and settle into the body.
Bring awareness to the base of the spine — feel it as a center.
Rotate upward: sacral, solar plexus, heart, throat, brow, crown.
Spend several breaths at each center.
End with awareness of all seven as one vertical field of light.

session_steps.title: Root
session_steps.content: Base of spine — feel the first center.

session_steps.title: Ascend
session_steps.content: Rotate upward through all seven centers.

session_steps.title: Each Center
session_steps.content: Several breaths at each.

session_steps.title: Field
session_steps.content: All seven as one vertical field.

content.expected_experience: The subtle body becomes palpable. Many feel warmth, tingling, or spaciousness along the spine.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Subtle sensations are normal; force nothing.

content.objective: Rotate awareness through the seven energy centers in deep rest. (Deep variation.)
instructions: Lie down and settle into the body.
Bring awareness to the base of the spine — feel it as a center.
Rotate upward: sacral, solar plexus, heart, throat, brow, crown.
Spend several breaths at each center.
End with awareness of all seven as one vertical field of light.

session_steps.title: Field
session_steps.content: All seven as one vertical field.

content.expected_experience: The subtle body becomes palpable. Many feel warmth, tingling, or spaciousness along the spine.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Subtle sensations are normal; force nothing.

title: Nidra for Pain
description: Use yoga nidra's rotation to change the relationship with chronic pain.
short_description: Use yoga nidra's rotation to change the relationship with ch

content.objective: Use yoga nidra's rotation to change the relationship with chronic pain.
instructions: Lie down in a position that is as comfortable as possible.
Rotate awareness through the body — including, gently, the painful region.
Describe the pain neutrally: location, quality, edges.
Notice the pain is one sensation among many — not the whole body.
End with the sankalpa: 'I am more than this sensation.'

session_steps.title: Comfort
session_steps.content: Find the most comfortable possible position.

session_steps.title: Rotate
session_steps.content: Full body rotation — including the painful area, gently.

session_steps.title: Neutral
session_steps.content: Describe the pain without story.

session_steps.title: Context
session_steps.content: Pain is one sensation among many. Sankalpa: 'I am more than this sensation.'

content.expected_experience: Pain is not removed, but its empire shrinks. The body is rediscovered as mostly non-painful — a crucial rebalancing.
contraindications: undiagnosed pain — see a physician first
acute injury — skip the painful region
content.safety_notes: Never practice on acute pain. For chronic pain, include the region gently — avoidance teaches the brain the pain is enormous. If intensity spikes, move attention away and return slowly.

title: The Descending Ladder
description: A countdown structure that carries awareness down into deep rest.
short_description: A countdown structure that carries awareness down into deep

content.objective: A countdown structure that carries awareness down into deep rest.
instructions: Lie down and close your eyes.
Begin at 27. With each number, feel yourself descending.
Each number is one step down a ladder into rest.
If you lose count, begin again at 27 — no frustration.
By the time you reach 1, the body is deeply still.

session_steps.title: Top
session_steps.content: Begin at 27.

session_steps.title: Descend
session_steps.content: One number per breath — descending.

session_steps.title: Reset
session_steps.content: Lost count? Back to 27, gently.

session_steps.title: Bottom
session_steps.content: At 1, rest in the stillness.

content.expected_experience: The countdown gives the busy mind a task it accepts — and the descent happens almost unnoticed.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Awareness of Sleep Itself
description: The advanced nidra — watching the transition into sleep without losing awareness.
short_description: The advanced nidra — watching the transition into sleep with

content.objective: The advanced nidra — watching the transition into sleep without losing awareness.
instructions: Lie down at night, intending to stay aware.
Watch the process of falling asleep: thoughts thin, body fades.
Keep a faint thread of awareness on the fading itself.
If you fall asleep, the seed is planted for tonight.
Over nights, the thread strengthens — hypnagogic awareness grows.

session_steps.title: Intend
session_steps.content: Lie down with the intention to remain aware.

session_steps.title: Watch Fading
session_steps.content: Observe thoughts thinning, body fading.

session_steps.title: Thread
session_steps.content: Keep a faint thread on the transition.

session_steps.title: Seed
session_steps.content: Sleep is fine — the seed is planted.

content.expected_experience: The threshold of sleep becomes visible. This is the practice behind lucid dreaming and the yoga of sleep — patience rewarded over weeks.
content.safety_notes: Do not fight sleep. The practice is observation of the threshold, not insomnia. If sleep deprivation results, practice earlier in the evening.

title: Systematic Body Scan
description: Bring awareness to each body region without judgment — the foundational somatic practice.
short_description: Bring awareness to each body region without judgment — the f

content.objective: Bring awareness to each body region without judgment — the foundational somatic practice.
instructions: Lie down comfortably. Close your eyes.
Bring attention to the feet. Feel whatever is there.
Move slowly upward: calves, knees, thighs, pelvis, belly, chest, back, hands, arms, shoulders, neck, face, crown.
Notice without changing. Sensation is data, not a problem.
End by feeling the whole body as one field.

session_steps.title: Feet
session_steps.content: Begin at the feet. Feel whatever is present.

session_steps.title: Ascend
session_steps.content: Slow sweep upward through every region.

session_steps.title: No Change
session_steps.content: Notice without changing — data, not project.

session_steps.title: Whole Field
session_steps.content: Feel the whole body as one field of sensation.

content.expected_experience: The body reveals itself as a living landscape. Chronic tensions become visible — and often soften simply by being seen.
content.safety_notes: If a region is numb, note 'numb' and move on. Numbness is also sensation. Do not force feeling.

title: The Weight of the Body
description: Feel the body's weight fully supported — a direct route to physical surrender.
short_description: Feel the body's weight fully supported — a direct route to p

content.objective: Feel the body's weight fully supported — a direct route to physical surrender.
instructions: Lie down on a firm surface.
Feel the weight of the body pressing into the floor.
Let the floor hold everything. You do not need to hold yourself up.
Notice where the body still braces against support.
Invite those spots to be held too.

session_steps.title: Floor
session_steps.content: Feel the body's weight meeting the floor.

session_steps.title: Support
session_steps.content: The floor holds everything — surrender to it.

session_steps.title: Brace
session_steps.content: Find the bracing spots. Invite them to be held.

session_steps.title: Sink
session_steps.content: Rest as weight fully supported.

content.expected_experience: Physical surrender arrives through support, not effort. The body's habitual bracing becomes visible and optional.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Use a mat if the floor is hard.

title: Boundary Awareness
description: Feel the skin as the boundary between self and world — and its permeability.
short_description: Feel the skin as the boundary between self and world — and i

content.objective: Feel the skin as the boundary between self and world — and its permeability.
instructions: Sit or stand comfortably.
Feel the skin — the boundary surface of the body.
Notice air touching skin: the boundary is also a meeting place.
Feel where 'inside' ends and 'outside' begins — and how fuzzy that edge is.
Rest as the boundary itself: neither fully separate nor fully merged.

session_steps.title: Skin
session_steps.content: Feel the skin as a surface.

session_steps.title: Meeting
session_steps.content: Air touches skin — boundary as meeting place.

session_steps.title: Fuzzy Edge
session_steps.content: Notice how permeable the inside/outside line really is.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Rest as the boundary.

content.expected_experience: The skin-edge becomes a philosophical experience — separation and connection discovered to be two views of one surface.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Internal Landscape
description: Explore the body's interior — organs, cavities, spaces — as felt geography.
short_description: Explore the body's interior — organs, cavities, spaces — as

content.objective: Explore the body's interior — organs, cavities, spaces — as felt geography.
instructions: Sit quietly. Bring attention inside the body.
Feel the chest cavity — heart, lungs, the space they occupy.
Feel the belly — stomach, intestines, the gut's own intelligence.
Feel the pelvis — the body's bowl.
You are not visualizing; you are feeling the body from inside.

session_steps.title: Inside
session_steps.content: Move attention inside the body.

session_steps.title: Chest
session_steps.content: Feel the chest cavity.

session_steps.title: Belly
session_steps.content: Feel the belly's organs and space.

session_steps.title: Geography
session_steps.content: Rest as the body's interior landscape.

content.expected_experience: Interoception deepens. The body stops being a shell and becomes a lived interior world — the foundation of somatic intelligence.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If internal attention triggers discomfort, return to the skin's surface — outer awareness is equally valid.

title: Posture Awareness
description: Notice posture as a live event — not a position but a continuous balancing act.
short_description: Notice posture as a live event — not a position but a contin

content.objective: Notice posture as a live event — not a position but a continuous balancing act.
instructions: Sit or stand as you normally would.
Feel the spine's subtle sways — posture is never static.
Notice the constant micro-adjustments keeping you upright.
Watch the adjustments without correcting them.
Then, gently, let posture improve itself — from awareness, not effort.

session_steps.title: Normal
session_steps.content: Adopt your ordinary posture.

session_steps.title: Sways
session_steps.content: Feel the constant micro-movements.

session_steps.title: No Correction
session_steps.content: Watch adjustments without fixing.

session_steps.title: Self-Organize
session_steps.content: Let posture improve from awareness alone.

content.expected_experience: Posture is discovered to be a verb, not a noun. Awareness alone often reorganizes alignment better than willpower.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Gait Awareness
description: Bring full attention to walking's mechanics — the most practiced movement of your life.
short_description: Bring full attention to walking's mechanics — the most pract

content.objective: Bring full attention to walking's mechanics — the most practiced movement of your life.
instructions: Walk at a normal pace.
Feel the heel strike, the roll through the sole, the toe push-off.
Feel the arms swing, the pelvis rotate, the head balance.
Notice: walking is a continuous act of falling and catching.
Let attention ride the movement like a wave.

session_steps.title: Walk
session_steps.content: Begin walking at normal pace.

session_steps.title: Foot
session_steps.content: Heel, roll, toe — the foot's story.

session_steps.title: Whole
session_steps.content: Arms, pelvis, head — the whole gait.

session_steps.title: Falling
session_steps.content: Walking as controlled falling. Rest in the wave.

content.expected_experience: Walking becomes fascinating — a skill so automatic it was invisible. Attention reveals its elegance.
content.safety_notes: Walk on safe ground with eyes open. Urban walking requires environmental awareness — the practice includes it.

title: Two-Hand Awareness
description: A precise micro-somatic practice — feel each hand separately, then together.
short_description: A precise micro-somatic practice — feel each hand separately

instructions: Rest hands on the knees, palms down.
Feel the left hand alone — every finger, the palm, the back.
Feel the right hand alone.
Feel both hands as one field.
Notice how attention itself changes the hands' vividness.

session_steps.title: Left
session_steps.content: Feel the left hand in detail.

session_steps.title: Right
session_steps.content: Feel the right hand in detail.

session_steps.title: Both
session_steps.content: Both hands as one field.

session_steps.title: Vividness
session_steps.content: Notice attention's effect on sensation.

content.expected_experience: A small practice with a big lesson: attention literally brightens sensation. The body is more available than assumed.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: The Body as Weather Map
description: Read emotional weather through the body's sensations.
short_description: Read emotional weather through the body's sensations.

content.objective: Read emotional weather through the body's sensations.
instructions: Sit quietly. Ask: what is the body's weather right now?
Scan for tension, warmth, tightness, openness, flutter, heaviness.
Map each sensation to a region — without interpreting why.
The body reports continuously; this practice reads the report.
End by feeling the whole weather system at once.

session_steps.title: Ask
session_steps.content: 'What is the body's weather?'

session_steps.title: Scan
session_steps.content: Tension, warmth, tightness, openness — region by region.

session_steps.title: Map
session_steps.content: Map sensations without interpreting causes.

session_steps.title: System
session_steps.content: Feel the whole weather system.

content.expected_experience: The body becomes a reliable instrument. Emotional patterns are caught earlier — at the sensation stage, before the story stage.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If the weather map reveals stormy regions, note them without diving into content — this is reading, not processing.

title: Face Release Scan
description: Release the face's habitual holding — the most expressive and most clenched region.
short_description: Release the face's habitual holding — the most expressive an

content.objective: Release the face's habitual holding — the most expressive and most clenched region.
instructions: Sit comfortably. Bring attention to the face.
Feel the forehead, the eyes, the jaw, the tongue, the throat.
Notice what is clenched — often without your knowing.
Invite each region to soften. The jaw and tongue especially.
Feel the face become a relaxed mask — expression without holding.

session_steps.title: Soften
session_steps.content: Invite each region to release.

content.expected_experience: The face holds years of micro-stress. Releasing it changes the whole body's tone — and often the mood follows.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. The jaw release alone is worth the practice.

title: Left-Right Asymmetry
description: Discover the body's natural asymmetry — and stop chasing symmetry.
short_description: Discover the body's natural asymmetry — and stop chasing sym

content.objective: Discover the body's natural asymmetry — and stop chasing symmetry.
instructions: Sit or stand. Feel the left side of the body.
Feel the right side.
Compare: weight, temperature, tension, aliveness.
Notice the differences without correcting them.
Asymmetry is not imbalance — it is the body's honest signature.

session_steps.title: Left
session_steps.content: Feel the left side fully.

session_steps.title: Right
session_steps.content: Feel the right side fully.

session_steps.title: Compare
session_steps.content: Weight, temperature, tension, aliveness.

session_steps.title: Accept
session_steps.content: Asymmetry as signature, not flaw.

content.expected_experience: The body's lopsidedness becomes interesting rather than wrong. Many report immediate postural relief from accepting asymmetry.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Root Grounding
description: Activate muladhara — the root center — for stability and safety.
short_description: Activate muladhara — the root center — for stability and saf

content.objective: Activate muladhara — the root center — for stability and safety.
instructions: Stand or sit with feet flat. Feel the floor.
Bring attention to the base of the spine.
Imagine roots descending from the pelvis into the earth.
With each exhale, sink the roots deeper.
Feel stability rise from below — grounded, not heavy.

session_steps.title: Feet
session_steps.content: Feel both feet meeting the floor.

session_steps.title: Base
session_steps.content: Attention at the base of the spine.

session_steps.title: Roots
session_steps.content: Imagine roots descending with each exhale.

session_steps.title: Stability
session_steps.content: Feel grounded stability rise upward.

content.expected_experience: A felt sense of being held by the earth — anxiety's antidote. Stability arrives from below, not from effort.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Standing grounding is also a first-aid tool for panic.

title: Sacral Flow
description: Open svadhisthana — the sacral center — to feel flow, pleasure, and creative movement.
short_description: Open svadhisthana — the sacral center — to feel flow, pleasu

content.objective: Open svadhisthana — the sacral center — to feel flow, pleasure, and creative movement.
instructions: Sit comfortably. Place both hands on the lower belly.
Breathe into the belly — let it move with the breath.
Imagine a warm, orange glow in the lower abdomen.
Add gentle hip circles or swaying, if seated freely.
Let the body's natural flow and pleasure return.

session_steps.title: Hands
session_steps.content: Hands on the lower belly.

session_steps.title: Breath
session_steps.content: Breathe into the belly; feel it move.

session_steps.title: Glow
session_steps.content: Imagine warm orange light in the lower abdomen.

session_steps.title: Flow
session_steps.content: Gentle sway or hip circles. Rest in flow.

content.expected_experience: The sacral center governs flow and pleasure. Practitioners often report a thawing of chronic pelvic holding.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Movements are gentle and optional — the breath alone carries the practice.

content.objective: Open svadhisthana — the sacral center — to feel flow, pleasure, and creative movement. (Gentle variation.)
instructions: Sit comfortably. Place both hands on the lower belly.
Breathe into the belly — let it move with the breath.
Imagine a warm, orange glow in the lower abdomen.
Add gentle hip circles or swaying, if seated freely.
Let the body's natural flow and pleasure return.

session_steps.title: Hands
session_steps.content: Hands on the lower belly.

session_steps.title: Breath
session_steps.content: Breathe into the belly; feel it move.

session_steps.title: Glow
session_steps.content: Imagine warm orange light in the lower abdomen.

session_steps.title: Flow
session_steps.content: Gentle sway or hip circles. Rest in flow.

content.expected_experience: The sacral center governs flow and pleasure. Practitioners often report a thawing of chronic pelvic holding.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Movements are gentle and optional — the breath alone carries the practice.

title: Solar Ignition
description: Activate manipura — the solar plexus — for willpower and confident action.
short_description: Activate manipura — the solar plexus — for willpower and con

content.objective: Activate manipura — the solar plexus — for willpower and confident action.
instructions: Sit erect. Place one hand on the upper abdomen.
Breathe deeply into the belly, feeling it press against the hand.
Imagine a bright yellow sun at the solar plexus.
With each exhale, feel the sun radiating warmth outward.
Set one small intention — the solar center responds to direction.

session_steps.title: Hand
session_steps.content: Hand on the solar plexus.

session_steps.title: Breath
session_steps.content: Deep belly breaths against the hand.

session_steps.title: Sun
session_steps.content: Visualize the yellow sun igniting.

session_steps.title: Intention
session_steps.content: One small intention. Feel the center respond.

content.expected_experience: The fire center warms — often felt as rising confidence and the energy to begin. Willpower has a physical seat.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If heat becomes agitation, lengthen the exhale to settle.

title: Heart Opening
description: Soften anahata — the heart center — into openness without vulnerability.
short_description: Soften anahata — the heart center — into openness without vu

content.objective: Soften anahata — the heart center — into openness without vulnerability.
instructions: Sit tall. Bring both hands to the center of the chest.
Feel the heartbeat or the chest's warmth.
With each inhale, imagine the chest widening — not forcing, allowing.
Recall one moment of genuine kindness — yours or another's.
Let the heart center stay open for the remaining breaths.

session_steps.title: Hands
session_steps.content: Hands at the center of the chest.

session_steps.title: Feel
session_steps.content: Feel heartbeat or chest warmth.

session_steps.title: Widen
session_steps.content: Inhale: the chest widens by allowance.

session_steps.title: Kindness
session_steps.content: Recall genuine kindness. Rest in openness.

content.expected_experience: The heart center opens not through sentiment but through permission. Many feel a physical warmth and a quiet courage.
content.safety_notes: If grief surfaces, let it — then ground at the feet. An open heart includes the full weather of feeling.

title: Throat Expression
description: Activate vishuddha — the throat center — for truthful, clear expression.
short_description: Activate vishuddha — the throat center — for truthful, clear

content.objective: Activate vishuddha — the throat center — for truthful, clear expression.
instructions: Sit tall. Feel the throat — swallow once, notice it.
Hum softly on the exhale: a comfortable 'hmmm'.
Feel the vibration in the throat.
Silently formulate one true thing you need to say.
Let the throat center feel open, resonant, ready.

session_steps.title: Throat
session_steps.content: Feel the throat; swallow once.

session_steps.title: Hum
session_steps.content: Soft humming on the exhale.

session_steps.title: Vibration
session_steps.content: Feel the hum's vibration.

session_steps.title: Truth
session_steps.content: Formulate one true thing to say. Rest in readiness.

content.expected_experience: The throat loosens — not for performance, but for truth. Expression begins as a physical openness.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Hum at any comfortable pitch. Skip if you have laryngitis.

title: Third Eye Clarity
description: Steady ajna — the brow center — for clarity of seeing and intuition.
short_description: Steady ajna — the brow center — for clarity of seeing and in

content.objective: Steady ajna — the brow center — for clarity of seeing and intuition.
instructions: Sit erect. Rest attention at the point between the eyebrows.
Soften the eyes and the forehead — no strain.
Imagine a steady, quiet light at the brow.
Ask one clear question. Let it rest at the brow without demanding an answer.
Notice the quality of inner seeing that arises.

session_steps.title: Brow
session_steps.content: Attention at the point between the eyebrows.

session_steps.title: Soften
session_steps.content: Soften eyes and forehead — no strain.

session_steps.title: Light
session_steps.content: Imagine a quiet, steady light.

session_steps.title: Question
session_steps.content: One clear question, held without demand. Notice inner seeing.

content.expected_experience: The brow center is the seat of inner seeing. Clarity arrives as quietness, not as lightning — patience is the practice.
content.safety_notes: If pressure or headache arises at the brow, move attention to the heart. The third eye is invited, never forced.

title: Crown Resting
description: Rest awareness at sahasrara — the crown — the center of pure openness.
short_description: Rest awareness at sahasrara — the crown — the center of pure

content.objective: Rest awareness at sahasrara — the crown — the center of pure openness.
instructions: Sit quietly. Let the head be balanced, not tilted.
Bring attention to the crown of the head — or just above it.
Imagine an open bowl, a lotus with a thousand petals, facing upward.
Nothing enters. Nothing leaves. Just openness resting on openness.
Stay for the session — the crown is rested, not worked.

session_steps.title: Balance
session_steps.content: Head balanced, spine tall.

session_steps.title: Crown
session_steps.content: Attention at the crown or just above.

session_steps.title: Open Bowl
session_steps.content: Imagine the thousand-petaled openness.

session_steps.title: Rest
session_steps.content: Openness resting on openness.

content.expected_experience: The crown center is not activated but rested — like lying down after a long journey. Many report a quiet, vast stillness.
content.safety_notes: If crown attention creates spaciness or fear, ground immediately: feet, floor, weight. The crown is always paired with the root.

title: Chakra Ladder
description: Ascend and descend the seven centers — a complete subtle-body tour.
short_description: Ascend and descend the seven centers — a complete subtle-bod

content.objective: Ascend and descend the seven centers — a complete subtle-body tour.
instructions: Sit tall. Begin at the base of the spine.
Ascend slowly: root, sacral, solar, heart, throat, brow, crown.
Pause at each center — feel its region, its color, its quality.
At the crown, rest. Then descend slowly back to the root.
The ladder up and down is one complete round. Do three.

session_steps.title: Root
session_steps.content: Begin at the base of the spine.

session_steps.title: Ascend
session_steps.content: Slow climb through all seven centers.

session_steps.title: Crown Rest
session_steps.content: Pause at the crown.

session_steps.title: Descend
session_steps.content: Slow return to the root. Three rounds.

content.expected_experience: The subtle body becomes a felt map. Regular ladder practice builds remarkable sensitivity to energy and mood shifts.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Move slowly — the ladder's value is in the pausing, not the climbing.

title: Paired Balancing
description: Balance lower and upper chakras — grounding and openness in one session.
short_description: Balance lower and upper chakras — grounding and openness in

content.objective: Balance lower and upper chakras — grounding and openness in one session.
instructions: Sit tall. Feel the root center — grounding, stability, earth.
Then feel the heart center — openness, warmth, connection.
Alternate: root, heart, root, heart — like a slow pendulum.
Let both centers be alive at once: rooted and open.
Rest in the balance — neither floating nor heavy.

session_steps.content: Rooted and open at once. Rest.

content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Kundalini Prep
description: Prepare the subtle body for awakening with purification and steadiness — never force.
short_description: Prepare the subtle body for awakening with purification and

content.objective: Prepare the subtle body for awakening with purification and steadiness — never force.
instructions: Sit erect. Begin with slow, even breathing.
Feel the spine as a hollow channel — from root to crown.
Imagine breath moving up the spine on the inhale, down on the exhale.
Keep everything gentle — awakening is invited, never pulled.
End by grounding: feel the feet, the floor, the weight of the body.

session_steps.title: Channel
session_steps.content: Feel the spine as a hollow channel.

title: Kundalini Prep — Evening
description: Prepare the subtle body for awakening with purification and steadiness — never force.
short_description: Prepare the subtle body for awakening with purification and

content.objective: Prepare the subtle body for awakening with purification and steadiness — never force. (Evening variation.)
instructions: Sit erect. Begin with slow, even breathing.
Feel the spine as a hollow channel — from root to crown.
Imagine breath moving up the spine on the inhale, down on the exhale.
Keep everything gentle — awakening is invited, never pulled.
End by grounding: feel the feet, the floor, the weight of the body.

title: Om Repetition
description: Vibrate the primordial sound — om — to still the mind and open the chest.
short_description: Vibrate the primordial sound — om — to still the mind and op

content.objective: Vibrate the primordial sound — om — to still the mind and open the chest.
instructions: Sit tall. Inhale fully.
Chant om on the exhale — a-u-m, three distinct resonances.
Feel the vibration in the chest, throat, and head.
Let the silence after each om be as long as the sound.
Repeat for the session. The sound does the work.

session_steps.title: Inhale
session_steps.content: Full inhale, tall spine.

session_steps.title: Chant
session_steps.content: Om on the exhale — a-u-m, three resonances.

session_steps.title: Vibration
session_steps.content: Feel the sound in chest, throat, head.

session_steps.title: Silence
session_steps.content: Let the silence after om be equal to the sound.

content.expected_experience: Om is the most studied mantra in contemplative science — its vibration is felt physically within minutes, and the mind quiets around it.
content.safety_notes: Chant at any comfortable volume. Whispered or mental om is equally valid when voice tires.

title: So Ham — I Am That
description: Ride the breath's own mantra — so ham — the sound of awareness itself.
short_description: Ride the breath's own mantra — so ham — the sound of awarene

content.objective: Ride the breath's own mantra — so ham — the sound of awareness itself.
instructions: Breathe naturally through the nose.
On the inhale, mentally hear 'so'.
On the exhale, mentally hear 'ham'.
So ham — 'I am That' — rides every breath you take.
Let the mantra and breath become indistinguishable.

session_steps.title: Breath
session_steps.content: Natural breathing through the nose.

session_steps.title: So
session_steps.content: Inhale: mentally hear 'so'.

session_steps.title: Ham
session_steps.content: Exhale: mentally hear 'ham'.

session_steps.title: One
session_steps.content: Mantra and breath become one movement.

content.expected_experience: The breath itself becomes the practice — 21,600 times a day, the body already chants. This practice simply makes it conscious.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. The mantra is mental; the breath stays natural.

title: Om Namah Shivaya
description: The five-syllable mantra of auspiciousness — a complete yoga in sound.
short_description: The five-syllable mantra of auspiciousness — a complete yoga

content.objective: The five-syllable mantra of auspiciousness — a complete yoga in sound.
instructions: Sit tall. Take one settling breath.
Chant aloud or whisper: om namah shivaya.
Let the five syllables land fully — na-mah-shi-va-ya.
Each round is one complete cycle of the mantra.
When the voice tires, continue silently.

session_steps.title: Settle
session_steps.content: One settling breath.

session_steps.title: Chant
session_steps.content: Om namah shivaya — aloud or whispered.

session_steps.title: Syllables
session_steps.content: Let all five syllables land fully.

session_steps.title: Silent
session_steps.content: Continue silently when the voice tires.

content.expected_experience: The panchakshari — five-syllable mantra — is a complete practice: it names the divine as the auspicious one within. Rounds accumulate quietly.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Any pace works — slow is better.

title: Gayatri Rhythm
description: The ancient Gayatri mantra — light for the intellect, practiced with respect for its lineage.
short_description: The ancient Gayatri mantra — light for the intellect, practi

content.objective: The ancient Gayatri mantra — light for the intellect, practiced with respect for its lineage.
instructions: Sit tall with reverence for the tradition.
Chant: om bhur bhuvaḥ svaḥ, tat savitur vareṇyaṃ, bhargo devasya dhīmahi, dhiyo yo naḥ prachodayāt.
Let the rhythm be slow — the Gayatri is savored, not rushed.
Its meaning: may the light of the sun of knowledge illuminate our intellect.
End in silence — the silence after is the mantra's fruit.

session_steps.title: Reverence
session_steps.content: Sit tall. Honor the lineage.

session_steps.title: Chant
session_steps.content: The Gayatri, slowly, in full.

session_steps.title: Meaning
session_steps.content: Hold the meaning: light illuminating the intellect.

session_steps.title: Silence
session_steps.content: End in silence — the fruit.

content.expected_experience: The Gayatri is thousands of years old and still practiced daily by millions. Its rhythm is engineered for the mind's settling.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Traditionally practiced at dawn, dusk, and noon — any consistent time works.

title: Maha Mantra
description: The great mantra of the names — Hare Krishna, Hare Rama — sung for the heart.
short_description: The great mantra of the names — Hare Krishna, Hare Rama — su

content.objective: The great mantra of the names — Hare Krishna, Hare Rama — sung for the heart.
instructions: Sit comfortably. Let the posture be easy.
Sing or chant: hare krishna, hare krishna, krishna krishna, hare hare / hare rama, hare rama, rama rama, hare hare.
Let the rhythm be musical — the maha mantra is meant to be sung.
Feel the names as sound, not as concepts.
When the voice rests, let the mind continue humming.

session_steps.title: Sing
session_steps.content: The maha mantra, in its full rhythm.

session_steps.title: Music
session_steps.content: Let it be sung, not recited.

session_steps.title: Hum
session_steps.content: The mind continues humming after the voice rests.

content.expected_experience: Kirtan-style chanting is among the most accessible devotional practices — the heart opens through sound before the mind understands.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Loud or soft, sung or whispered — all valid.

Let the rhythm be musical — the maha mantra is meant to be sung.
Feel the names as sound, not as concepts.
When the voice rests, let the mind continue humming.

session_steps.title: Easy
session_steps.content: Comfortable posture.

session_steps.title: Sing
session_steps.content: The maha mantra, in its full rhythm.

session_steps.title: Music
session_steps.content: Let it be sung, not recited.

session_steps.title: Hum
session_steps.content: The mind continues humming after the voice rests.

content.expected_experience: Kirtan-style chanting is among the most accessible devotional practices — the heart opens through sound before the mind understands.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Loud or soft, sung or whispered — all valid.

title: Lokah Samastah
description: The universal peace prayer — may all beings everywhere be happy and free.
short_description: The universal peace prayer — may all beings everywhere be ha

content.objective: The universal peace prayer — may all beings everywhere be happy and free.
instructions: Sit with an open heart.
Chant: lokah samastah sukhino bhavantu.
Its meaning: may all beings in all worlds be happy and free.
Extend the intention outward — family, city, country, all beings.
Let the chant be a radiation, not a request.

session_steps.title: Open Heart
session_steps.content: Settle with openness.

session_steps.title: Chant
session_steps.content: Lokah samastah sukhino bhavantu.

session_steps.title: Meaning
session_steps.content: May all beings everywhere be happy and free.

session_steps.title: Radiate
session_steps.content: Extend outward — family, city, all beings.

content.expected_experience: Compassion practice in mantra form. The scope of the wish — all beings, all worlds — gradually becomes the felt scope of the heart.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

short_description: Om gum ganapataye namaha — the remover of obstacles, invoked

content.objective: Om gum ganapataye namaha — the remover of obstacles, invoked at beginnings.
instructions: Sit tall. Begin any new undertaking with this practice.
Chant: om gum ganapataye namaha.
Feel the 'gum' resonating in the belly — the seed sound.
Set your intention for the session or the day.
The mantra is traditionally invoked before starting anything new.

title: Silent Mantra
description: Mental japa — the subtlest mantra practice, without sound or movement.
short_description: Mental japa — the subtlest mantra practice, without sound or

content.objective: Mental japa — the subtlest mantra practice, without sound or movement.
instructions: Sit quietly. Choose a mantra: om, so ham, or any word of power for you.
Repeat it silently — no lip movement, no sound.
Let the mantra be heard in the mind's ear.
When the mind wanders, the mantra retrieves it.
Silent repetition is considered the most potent form of japa.

session_steps.title: Choose
session_steps.content: One mantra, chosen simply.

session_steps.title: Silent
session_steps.content: Repeat mentally — no sound, no movement.

session_steps.title: Mind's Ear
session_steps.content: Hear it internally.

session_steps.title: Retrieve
session_steps.content: The mantra retrieves wandering attention.

content.expected_experience: Mental japa builds extraordinary concentration. The mantra becomes a constant, quiet companion available in any moment of life.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If the mind resists silence, begin with whispered japa and graduate to mental.

title: Mala Counting 108
description: Complete one full mala — 108 repetitions — using the traditional counting method.
short_description: Complete one full mala — 108 repetitions — using the traditi

content.objective: Complete one full mala — 108 repetitions — using the traditional counting method.
instructions: Hold the mala in the right hand, draped over the middle finger.
Use the thumb to move one bead per repetition.
The guru bead is not counted — stop there, reverse direction.
Keep the mantra steady, the pace unhurried.
One full round of 108 is a complete practice.

session_steps.title: Hold
session_steps.content: Mala in the right hand, beads on the middle finger.

session_steps.title: Move
session_steps.content: Thumb moves one bead per repetition.

session_steps.title: Guru Bead
session_steps.content: Stop at the guru bead; reverse direction.

session_steps.title: Complete
session_steps.content: 108 repetitions — one full round.

content.expected_experience: The mala's physicality anchors the mind — fingers moving, beads felt. 108 repetitions take about 15-20 minutes and reliably induce calm focus.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. The mala is a tool, not a talisman — its power is in the repetition.

title: Finger Japa
description: Japa without a mala — using the fingers themselves as the counting field.
short_description: Japa without a mala — using the fingers themselves as the co

content.objective: Japa without a mala — using the fingers themselves as the counting field.
instructions: No mala needed. Use the thumb to touch each finger in sequence.
Index, middle, ring, little — one round of four.
Then reverse: little, ring, middle, index.
Each touch is one repetition of the mantra.
Count rounds rather than beads — ten rounds is a solid session.

session_steps.title: Sequence
session_steps.content: Thumb touches index, middle, ring, little.

session_steps.title: Forward
session_steps.content: One round of four touches.

session_steps.title: Reverse
session_steps.content: Return: little to index.

session_steps.title: Rounds
session_steps.content: Ten rounds completes the session.

content.expected_experience: The most portable japa — possible in any posture, any place. The fingers become a mala always with you.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Whispered Japa
description: Upamsu japa — the middle volume between loud and silent.
short_description: Upamsu japa — the middle volume between loud and silent.

content.objective: Upamsu japa — the middle volume between loud and silent.
instructions: Sit comfortably. Begin the mantra at a whisper.
The lips move, the voice is barely audible.
Feel the mantra in the throat and mouth.
Whispering occupies the speech faculty, quieting inner chatter.
When tired, drop to mental japa.

session_steps.title: Whisper
session_steps.content: Begin the mantra at whisper volume.

session_steps.title: Lips
session_steps.content: Feel the lips and throat engage.

session_steps.title: Occupy
session_steps.content: Whispering occupies the speech faculty.

session_steps.title: Drop
session_steps.content: Tired? Continue mentally.

content.expected_experience: Whispered japa is the traditional recommendation when the mind is too restless for mental repetition — the body's involvement steadies attention.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Whispering for long periods can tire the voice — hydrate and rest.

title: Loud Japa
description: Vaikhari japa — full-voiced chanting for when the mind is stormy.
short_description: Vaikhari japa — full-voiced chanting for when the mind is st

content.objective: Vaikhari japa — full-voiced chanting for when the mind is stormy.
instructions: Sit tall. Begin chanting the mantra aloud.
Let the voice be full but not strained.
Feel the vibration in the chest and skull.
Loud japa drowns the mind's noise with its own sound.
When the storm settles, lower the volume gradually.

session_steps.title: Aloud
session_steps.content: Chant the mantra at full voice.

session_steps.title: Vibration
session_steps.content: Feel chest and skull resonance.

session_steps.title: Drown
session_steps.content: The mantra's sound covers the mind's noise.

session_steps.title: Lower
session_steps.content: Gradually reduce volume as calm arrives.

content.expected_experience: Loud chanting is remarkably effective against agitation — the vocal apparatus absorbs the mind's energy and returns it as vibration.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Do not shout — projection, not volume. Stop if the voice hurts.

content.objective: Bind the mantra to the breath — one repetition per breath cycle.
instructions: Breathe naturally through the nose.

Complete it on the exhale — one mantra per breath.
The breath becomes the metronome of repetition.
When breath and mantra synchronize, attention stabilizes.

session_steps.content: Natural nasal breathing.

session_steps.title: Inhale
session_steps.content: Begin the mantra on the inhale.

session_steps.title: Exhale
session_steps.content: Complete it on the exhale.

session_steps.title: Sync
session_steps.content: Breath and mantra lock together.

content.expected_experience: Binding mantra to breath unites the two great concentration technologies. The mind has nowhere to go — and goes quiet.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Never strain the breath to fit the mantra — the mantra fits the breath.

title: Japa for Anxiety
description: Use the mantra's rhythm to interrupt anxiety's spiral.
short_description: Use the mantra's rhythm to interrupt anxiety's spiral.

content.objective: Use the mantra's rhythm to interrupt anxiety's spiral.
instructions: Sit or stand — any position works.
Begin a slow mantra: om shanti, or so ham.
Let the mantra's pace set the nervous system's pace.
Anxiety's thoughts continue; the mantra rides over them.
Continue until the breath visibly slows.

session_steps.title: Any Position
session_steps.content: Sit or stand — begin immediately.

session_steps.title: Slow Mantra
session_steps.content: Om shanti or so ham, slow.

session_steps.title: Rhythm
session_steps.content: The mantra sets the nervous system's tempo.

session_steps.title: Slow Breath
session_steps.content: Continue until the breath visibly slows.

content.expected_experience: Rhythmic repetition is one of the fastest non-pharmacological anxiety interventions — the pattern itself is regulating.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. If anxiety escalates despite japa, switch to grounding: feet, floor, five things you can see.

title: Japa for Sleep
description: A bedtime japa that carries the mind toward sleep's threshold.
short_description: A bedtime japa that carries the mind toward sleep's threshol

content.objective: A bedtime japa that carries the mind toward sleep's threshold.
instructions: Lie down in bed, lights off.
Begin a slow, silent mantra: om, or om shanti.
Let each repetition be slower and softer than the last.
The mantra is a ferry — you are not rowing, you are riding.
Sleep is the destination. Falling asleep mid-japa is success.

session_steps.title: Bed
session_steps.content: Lie down, lights off.

session_steps.title: Silent
session_steps.content: Slow, silent mantra begins.

session_steps.title: Slower
session_steps.content: Each repetition slower, softer.

session_steps.title: Ferry
session_steps.content: Ride the mantra toward sleep.

content.expected_experience: The mantra gives the racing mind a task it accepts — and the task itself is soporific. Many practitioners fall asleep before the session ends.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. This is a sleep practice — do not practice it while driving.

title: Japa with Sankalpa
description: Plant a resolve into the field of repetition — japa with direction.
short_description: Plant a resolve into the field of repetition — japa with dir

content.objective: Plant a resolve into the field of repetition — japa with direction.
instructions: Begin japa as usual — mantra and counting.
After the first round, state your sankalpa silently.
One sentence, positive, present tense: 'I am calm.'
Continue japa, letting the sankalpa ride the repetitions.
End by releasing the sankalpa — planted, not clutched.

session_steps.title: Begin
session_steps.content: Start japa normally.

session_steps.title: Sankalpa
session_steps.content: After round one, state the resolve silently.

session_steps.title: Ride
session_steps.content: The sankalpa rides the repetitions.

session_steps.title: Release
session_steps.content: End by releasing it — planted, not clutched.

content.expected_experience: Repetition plus intention is the classic formula for deep planting — the sankalpa reaches the soil where habits grow.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Formulate sankalpa positively — the mind plants what it hears.

title: Mantra Mala Marathon
description: Multiple mala rounds — building stamina in attention and devotion.
short_description: Multiple mala rounds — building stamina in attention and dev

content.objective: Multiple mala rounds — building stamina in attention and devotion.
instructions: Set a timer for 30 minutes.
Begin japa with the mala. Complete round after round.
When the guru bead is reached, reverse and continue.
Restlessness will come and go — the mala keeps counting.
End with three breaths of gratitude for the practice.

session_steps.title: Timer
session_steps.content: Set 30 minutes.

session_steps.title: Rounds
session_steps.content: Round after round — the mala keeps count.

session_steps.title: Reverse
session_steps.content: At the guru bead, reverse direction.

session_steps.title: Gratitude
session_steps.content: End with three breaths of gratitude.

content.expected_experience: Extended japa reveals attention's true texture — boredom, resistance, and eventually a strange, sweet absorption that short sessions never reach.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Take breaks if the hand tires — the count continues mentally.

title: Classic Candle Trataka
description: Steady, unblinking candle gazing — the classical trataka.
short_description: Steady, unblinking candle gazing — the classical trataka.

content.objective: Steady, unblinking candle gazing — the classical trataka.
instructions: Place a candle at eye level, an arm's length away, in a dim room.
Gaze at the flame's center — steady, unblinking.
When the eyes water or tire, close them gently.
Hold the afterimage at the eyebrow center.
Repeat the cycle for the session.

session_steps.title: Candle
session_steps.content: Eye level, arm's length, dim room.

session_steps.title: Gaze
session_steps.content: Steady, unblinking focus on the flame's center.

session_steps.title: Close
session_steps.content: Close when eyes tire; hold the afterimage.

session_steps.title: Cycle
session_steps.content: Repeat gaze-close cycles.

content.expected_experience: Trataka is called 'the lamp of concentration' — afterimage work trains the mind to hold what the eyes release.
content.safety_notes: Never gaze at the sun. Candle only. Stop at eye strain.

session_steps.title: Gaze
session_steps.content: Steady, unblinking focus on the flame's center.

session_steps.title: Close
session_steps.content: Close when eyes tire; hold the afterimage.

session_steps.title: Cycle
session_steps.content: Repeat gaze-close cycles.

content.expected_experience: Trataka is called 'the lamp of concentration' — afterimage work trains the mind to hold what the eyes release.
content.safety_notes: Never gaze at the sun. Candle only. Stop at eye strain.

title: Dot Gazing
description: Trataka on a simple drawn dot — concentration without flame.
short_description: Trataka on a simple drawn dot — concentration without flame.

content.objective: Trataka on a simple drawn dot — concentration without flame.
instructions: Draw a small dot on paper at eye level.
Gaze steadily without blinking.
Let the dot become the entire visual world.
Close the eyes; hold the dot's afterimage.
Repeat until the afterimage holds steadily.

session_steps.title: Dot
session_steps.content: A small dot at eye level.

session_steps.title: Gaze
session_steps.content: Steady, unblinking.

session_steps.title: World
session_steps.content: The dot becomes the whole visual field.

session_steps.title: Afterimage
session_steps.content: Close eyes; hold the dot internally.

content.expected_experience: The dot is the candle's minimal cousin — same concentration, no fire. Ideal for offices and travel.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Blink naturally when needed.

title: Water Gazing
description: Trataka on still water — the reflective surface as teacher.
short_description: Trataka on still water — the reflective surface as teacher.

content.objective: Trataka on still water — the reflective surface as teacher.
instructions: Fill a bowl with water. Place it at eye level.
Gaze at the water's surface without touching it.
Watch the reflections and the stillness beneath them.
Notice how the mind settles watching water settle.
Close the eyes; hold the water's image.

session_steps.title: Bowl
session_steps.content: Still water in a bowl, eye level.

session_steps.title: Surface
session_steps.content: Gaze at the surface.

session_steps.title: Beneath
session_steps.content: Notice stillness beneath reflections.

session_steps.title: Image
session_steps.content: Close eyes; hold the water's image.

content.expected_experience: Water gazing is ancient and cross-cultural. The mind mirrors the water — watching still water stills the watcher.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all. Spills happen — place the bowl on a tray.

title: Flame Visualization
description: Internal trataka — recreating the flame entirely in the mind's eye.
short_description: Internal trataka — recreating the flame entirely in the mind

content.objective: Internal trataka — recreating the flame entirely in the mind's eye.
instructions: Gaze at a candle for one minute.
Close the eyes. Recreate the flame internally.
Watch its flicker, its colors, its movement.
When the internal flame fades, glance again — then close.
The internal flame becomes steadier than the real one.

session_steps.title: One Minute
session_steps.content: Gaze at the candle.

session_steps.title: Close
session_steps.content: Recreate the flame internally.

session_steps.title: Flicker
session_steps.content: Watch its colors and movement.

session_steps.title: Refresh
session_steps.content: Faded? Glance, close, recreate.

content.expected_experience: The mind's eye learns to hold a stable image — a skill that transfers to every visualization practice.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all with normal candle precautions.

title: Moon Gazing
description: Trataka under moonlight — the traditional cooling practice.
short_description: Trataka under moonlight — the traditional cooling practice.

content.objective: Trataka under moonlight — the traditional cooling practice.
instructions: Sit comfortably facing the moon — any phase works.
Gaze softly at the moon or its light on the ground.
Do not stare at the moon itself for long — soft gaze.
Feel the cool, silver quality of moonlight attention.
Close the eyes; hold the silver afterimage.

session_steps.title: Face
session_steps.content: Sit facing the moon.

session_steps.title: Soft Gaze
session_steps.content: Soft gaze at moonlight.

session_steps.title: Cool
session_steps.content: Feel the cooling quality.

session_steps.title: Silver
session_steps.content: Close eyes; hold the silver image.

content.expected_experience: Moon gazing is traditionally prescribed for calming excess heat — anger, inflammation, restlessness. The practice itself is gentle and slow.
content.safety_notes: Never gaze directly at the sun. The moon is safe for soft gazing. Cloudy nights work too — gaze at the bright sky.

title: Yantra Gazing
description: Trataka on a geometric yantra — sacred geometry as concentration object.
short_description: Trataka on a geometric yantra — sacred geometry as concentra

content.objective: Trataka on a geometric yantra — sacred geometry as concentration object.
instructions: Place a yantra (or simple mandala) at eye level.
Gaze at its center point.
Let attention expand outward through the geometry — triangles, circles, petals.
Notice how the design leads the eye inward and outward simultaneously.
Close the eyes; hold the yantra's structure internally.

session_steps.title: Center
session_steps.content: Gaze at the yantra's center.

session_steps.title: Expand
session_steps.content: Attention moves outward through the geometry.

session_steps.title: In and Out
session_steps.content: The design leads the eye both ways.

session_steps.title: Internal
session_steps.content: Hold the structure with eyes closed.

content.expected_experience: Yantras are concentration machines — their geometry is engineered to organize attention. Gazing reveals why they've been used for millennia.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Trataka for Sleep
description: The sleep-entry trataka — gaze, close, fade.
short_description: The sleep-entry trataka — gaze, close, fade.

content.objective: The sleep-entry trataka — gaze, close, fade.
instructions: In bed, light a candle across the room.
Gaze softly at the flame for a minute or two.
Extinguish the candle.
Close the eyes and watch the afterimage fade.
The fading image carries you toward sleep.

session_steps.title: Candle
session_steps.content: A candle across the room, in bed.

session_steps.title: Soft Gaze
session_steps.content: One to two minutes of soft gazing.

session_steps.title: Extinguish
session_steps.content: Blow out the candle.

session_steps.title: Fade
session_steps.content: Watch the afterimage fade toward sleep.

content.expected_experience: The fading afterimage is a natural hypnotic — attention follows it down toward sleep. A beloved pre-sleep ritual.
content.safety_notes: Extinguish the candle before drowsiness sets in. Never sleep with a burning candle unattended.

title: Trataka for Concentration
description: The full concentration protocol — extended gazing with afterimage work.
short_description: The full concentration protocol — extended gazing with after

content.objective: The full concentration protocol — extended gazing with afterimage work.
instructions: Set a timer for 20 minutes.
Gaze at the candle without blinking as long as comfortable.
Close and hold the afterimage until it fades completely.
Repeat the cycle for the full session.
Track how long the unblinking gaze becomes over weeks.

session_steps.title: Timer
session_steps.content: Set 20 minutes.

session_steps.title: Gaze
session_steps.content: Unblinking as long as comfortable.

session_steps.title: Hold
session_steps.content: Afterimage held until complete fade.

session_steps.title: Track
session_steps.content: Log gaze duration over weeks.

content.expected_experience: This is trataka as athletic training — measurable progress in gaze duration and afterimage stability within weeks.
content.safety_notes: Stop at any eye discomfort. Progress is gradual — the eyes tire before the mind does.

description: Turn one ordinary cup of tea into a complete meditation.
short_description: Turn one ordinary cup of tea into a complete meditation.

content.objective: Turn one ordinary cup of tea into a complete meditation.

Take the first sip without speaking or reading.
Taste fully — temperature, texture, aftertaste.
Continue slowly. The cup empties; attention stays.

title: Mindful Walking
description: Walk with full attention on the feet — movement as meditation.
short_description: Walk with full attention on the feet — movement as meditatio

content.objective: Walk with full attention on the feet — movement as meditation.
instructions: Walk slowly, at half your normal pace.
Feel the lifting, moving, placing of each foot.
Let attention ride the soles.
When the mind wanders, the feet retrieve it.
Arrive at your destination having actually traveled.

session_steps.content: Attention rides the soles.

session_steps.title: Arrive
session_steps.content: Arrive having actually traveled.

content.expected_experience: Walking becomes the practice — no special posture, no cushion, just the road under attention.
content.safety_notes: Walk on safe ground, eyes open. Urban walking includes traffic awareness.

title: First Three Bites
description: Eat the first three bites of any meal in complete mindfulness.
short_description: Eat the first three bites of any meal in complete mindfulnes

content.objective: Eat the first three bites of any meal in complete mindfulness.
instructions: Before eating, pause. Look at the food.
Take the first bite without distraction — no phone, no conversation.
Chew slowly. Notice texture, temperature, flavor layers.
Repeat for three bites. Then eat normally.
Three mindful bites change the whole meal's digestion.

title: Mindful Listening
description: Listen to another person without planning your reply.
short_description: Listen to another person without planning your reply.

content.objective: Listen to another person without planning your reply.
instructions: In conversation, notice the impulse to reply.
Let the impulse pass. Keep listening.
Listen for the feeling beneath the words.
Notice the pauses — they are part of the speech.
When you speak, speak from what you heard.

session_steps.title: Pass
session_steps.content: Let it pass. Keep listening.

session_steps.title: Beneath

title: Mindful Waiting
description: Transform waiting — queues, lifts, loading screens — into practice.
short_description: Transform waiting — queues, lifts, loading screens — into pr

content.objective: Transform waiting — queues, lifts, loading screens — into practice.
instructions: The next time you wait, notice the resistance.
Feel the feet. Feel the breath.
Watch the impatience as a bodily event.
Waiting is most of life's unused time — reclaim it.
The queue ends; the practice continues.

session_steps.title: Resistance

session_steps.title: Feet and Breath
session_steps.content: Feel both.

session_steps.title: Impatience
session_steps.content: Watch it as a bodily event.

session_steps.title: Reclaim
session_steps.content: Waiting becomes practice.

content.expected_experience: Waiting stops being wasted time and becomes hundreds of micro-practices per week — the most available meditation in modern life.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.

title: Mindful Handwashing
description: The twenty-second ritual — handwashing as full awareness practice.
short_description: The twenty-second ritual — handwashing as full awareness pra

content.objective: The twenty-second ritual — handwashing as full awareness practice.
instructions: Turn on the water. Feel its temperature.
Feel the soap's texture, the lather forming.
Wash each finger deliberately.
Notice the water's sound and the rinse.
Dry slowly. The hands are clean and the mind is too.

session_steps.title: Water
session_steps.content: Feel temperature and flow.

session_steps.title: Soap
session_steps.content: Texture, lather, each finger.

session_steps.title: Rinse
session_steps.content: Sound and water.

session_steps.title: Dry
session_steps.content: Slowly. Clean hands, clean mind.

content.expected_experience: A practice so small it can't be skipped — and so complete it trains the same attention as an hour on the cushion.
content.safety_notes: Safe for all.
